Unmanaged litter fuels wildfires, slows nutrient cycling, and contributes to air pollution through burning. 

This Community-Oriented Management of Plant Organics for Socio-ecological Sustainability and Transformation (COMPOST) project develops a circular economy model to transform leaf litter into compost, creating a scalable forest-based enterprises tailored to Nepal’s context. Through collaboration with the government of Nepal, Divisional Forest Office, University and Community Forest User Groups, it advances contextually appropriate composting technologies and enterprises, trains and strengthens the capacities of the Community Forest User Groups and raises awareness of litter management opportunities in the forest fire hotspot district of Chure region Nepal."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: BioTransform: A Pilot Model for Waste Valorization for Small-Scale Kenyan Farmers to Enhance Energy Production, Soil Health, and Sustainable Agricultu
descriptions:
"Agriculture is the backbone of Kenya’s economy, with smallholder farmers in Kericho and Bomet Counties relying heavily on dairy and crop production. However, unsustainable farming practices, poor waste management, and rising input costs have led to environmental degradation, reduced productivity, and declining interest in agriculture among youth. 

This proposal aims to transform farm waste into valuable resources through household/farm biogas and composting pilot projects. By converting organic waste into biogas for energy and compost for soil enrichment, the initiative improves farm productivity, reduces greenhouse gas emissions, reduces waste, and creates new income streams. The pilot will serve as training hubs for farmers, demonstrating practical, low-cost solutions for waste-to-resource conversion. With support from county governments, farmer cooperatives, and women groups, the project will be scaled using a pay-as-you-go model to ensure affordability and sustainability for farmers to roll out."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Leveraging Digital Twins for Community-Driven Sustainable WEFE Nexus Management
descriptions: The project "Leveraging Digital Twins for Community-Driven Sustainable WEFE Nexus Management" thus rises from the growing pressures caused by urbanization, climate change, and resource scarcity at the heart of Jordan. The visionary initiative is the proposal for creating a digital twin—an interactive, all-pervasive, digital replica of Irbid, Jordan—designed to revolutionize how the Water-Energy-Food-Environment (WEFE) nexus is managed. Dr. Shehadeh, one of the leading professionals in the area of construction engineering with expertise in AI and Automation, will be in charge of this initiative and has promised that the latest and most sophisticated technology solutions—including Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, and artificial intelligence (AI)—will be employed in this initiative. This is the project's core - the ability to model the complex interrelations of the WEFE Nexus that would allow decision-makers, based on evidence-driven data, to reach sustainable, resilient, and fair decisions. It is through these above-mentioned provisions that this project is expected not only to optimize resource management but also to ensure the proper safekeeping of the rich cultural heritage of Irbid while stimulating local community participation. These transformations will follow the projected trajectory to an operational model of a digital twin of Irbid to aid the Nexus-based Urban Planning, enhanced resilience of water, energy, and food systems to the impacts of climate variability, conservation of valuable environmental resources, and empowerment of local communities to take the driving seat of their sustainable future. "Leveraging Digital Twins for Sustainable WEFE Nexus Management in Jordan" is not a project but a leap into setting a global precedent of technology interfacing with community and heritage to address 21st-century challenges. This promises to carve a way for sustainable urban development in Jordan and the world beyond, showing how digital twins can create a resilient, sustainable, and inclusive world that is resilient, sustainable, and inclusive. Malaysia faces several challenges in managing its infrastructure, such as aging infrastructure, scarce resources, and environmental harm. The outcomes of this project will not only support the Jordanian city, Irbid but also be transferable to cities in Malaysia.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Innovative approaches to Kenyan healthcare needs identification and impact pathways
descriptions:
Various factors collude to constrain access to critical medical devices for delivering hospital care in Africa. Specifically, access to equipment suited to local conditions for delivery of care in health facilities and effective maintenance solutions are major challenges. This is evidenced by extensive hospital equipment graveyards. Implications for critical hospital care are dire.
At the same time, talent in innovation and entrepreneurship focused on developing healthcare solutions is booming. However, despite the proliferation of mechanisms for converging ideas, talent and capital, there is little evidence of solutions progressing beyond the minimum viable product stage. Key reasons for this are twofold: (i) existing approaches to identification and prioritization of the greatest needs within hospital care are inadequate, and (ii) articulation of pathways for translating the need to a solution that will result in widespread normalised adoption within African health facilities remains a major challenge.
This proposal aims to address these issues by conducting a pilot study, as an initial step, in four Kenyan counties (Kajiado, Kiambu, Makueni and Nairobi). The project brings together an interdisciplinary team from four universities and two private sector partners. The combined expertise includes engineering, study design, economics of innovation, mathematical modeling and entrepreneurship.
The team will co-design a study, with stakeholders in the healthcare and medtech sectors, whose outputs will be (i) a validated prioritised list of healthcare needs (ii) a framework to determine “needs-fit” and (iii) a pathway to translate needs into commercial solutions. The research tools/study design will be informed and tested through key informant interviews. Validation of findings will be done via stakeholder engagement, followed by an additional iteration of the framework based on the validation workshop outcome.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Foundations for SADC -specific curriculum for transport infrastructure
descriptions: Countries in Southern Africa lag behind in terms of transport infrastructure which is also reflected on economic growth. Most countries in the region including Malawi have high logistics costs due to undeveloped water, road, rail and air transport infrastructure. These countries have policy documents that envision improved infrastructures but lack the springboard which is homegrown skilled human capacity. This calls for skills development through curriculum development and realignment. Several universities and colleges in the region have programs with transport infrastructure content but it is either outdated or lacks emphasis. Different stakeholders would be required for a successful curriculum framework for transport infrastructure in the region. This project proposes a workshop to develop a transport infrastructure curriculum framework for Southern Africa.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Revolutionize Engineering: Vision Infinity Student Vanguard (Kenya)
descriptions:
"Revolutionize Engineering: Vision Infinity Student Vanguard" was a transformative initiative that addressed the acute skills shortage in Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technologies across Africa, particularly in Kenya. The project empowered university and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) students with hands-on expertise in cutting-edge fields such as AI, VR, AR, and computer vision.

The objective of the Frontiers Impact Grant is to amplify the transformative outcomes of "Revolutionize Engineering: Vision Infinity Student Vanguard" by leveraging the power of storytelling through an impactful podcast series.his podcast will serve as the core communication strategy, using engaging narratives to highlight the real-life success stories of students applying their 4IR skills, the insights of industry leaders envisioning Africa’s potential, and the strategies of policymakers driving change.

The podcast will educate and inspire a global audience, galvanizing action among funders, policymakers, and industry stakeholders. By weaving together personal and professional stories, it will demonstrate the urgent need to invest in Africa’s youth and showcase how bridging the skills gap can position the continent as a global innovation hub.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Data Transformation for a Sustainable Net-zero Future.
descriptions: This policy dialogue focuses on the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven solutions in the global effort to achieve a sustainable, net-zero future. The aim of this policy dialogue is to raise awareness of the role of AI and data transformation in driving towards a sustainable net-zero future, facilitate discussion and collaboration between stakeholders on how to reduce environmental impact across various sectors, and identify and address the barriers to using AI and data transformation for net-zero. The event will bring together stakeholders from the local and regional community to discuss and collaborate on how to achieve a sustainable net-zero future. It will also raise awareness of the role of AI and data transformation in achieving net-zero and develop a roadmap for achieving net-zero in Malaysia. The event will benefit the local community by reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving air quality, and creating jobs in the green economy. Additionally, it will provide networking opportunities for stakeholders, including government, academia, industry, and non-governmental organizations. This event will serve as a foundation for local initiatives on climate action, creating an empowered community ready to address climate challenges using advanced technology.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Mapping of the WEFE Nexus within Refugee Camps in Jordan
descriptions:
Mapping technology has the potential to be a helpful tool in community building in informal settlements. Specifically, in refugee contexts, open-source participatory mapping technologies are seen as essential tools for early-stage disaster response and post-natural disaster community rebuilding activity . As camps evolve into permanent settlements, refugees become important stakeholders whose voices, opinions, and positions can be captured and negotiated for in community building through people-centered geospatial mapping.The present research aims to establish an interdisciplinary methodological framework for participatory mapping of the WEFE nexus in a case study of a Syrian refugee camp. The Za’atari Refugee Camp is the second largest camp in the world as reported by the UNHCR , hosting nearly 80,000 Syrian refugees and served by a network of 26 humanitarian service providers. Under the REACH Initiative, Za’atari camp became one of the most detailed mapped camps in the world, and under UNHCR coordination, mapping technologies have been used to conduct rapid camp assessments. However, the online mapping technology used in Za’atari, OpenStreetMap (OSM), has not kept up with the evolution of the camp, leading to many inconsistencies and gaps in the geospatial data. More critically, the engagement of the refugees themselves with camp management in joint decision making around resource use is not informed by shared mapping activities. Thus, the co-production of community maps of resource flows can help support the degree of order desired by camp managers without ignoring the self-organized leadership of the refugees.
The methodologies developed and refined at Za’atari Refugee Camp present a valuable blueprint for extending the approach to other, potentially more structurally and socially complex refugee communities across Jordan (such as Azraq and Al Baqa’a). Through strategic adaptation and upscaling, this approach has the potential to significantly impact refugee communities by addressing critical WEFE nexus challenges in a sustainable and

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: AI Governance and Safety: Understanding the Impacts of AI and Enabling Partnerships in the Philippines
descriptions:
This project aims to promote awareness and foster collaboration for artificial intelligence (AI) governance and safety in the Philippines, ensuring its benefits are harnessed while mitigating risks. The project will enhance awareness of AI governance, safety, and ethical considerations in developing and using AI among the various stakeholders in the government, industry, academia, and civil society. Deliver capacity-building workshops on AI governance and safety to the different stakeholders in the Philippines.
And engage in global collaboration and share best practices for AI governance and safety in the ASEAN region.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Advancing Energy Storage Solutions for Sustainable Energy Transitions in Thailand
descriptions: Recognising the pivotal role of energy storage in integrating renewable energy and ensuring grid stability, the project aims to address Thailand’s unique energy challenges.Through a series of webinars, workshops, summer school sessions, and active participation in international conferences, this initiative seeks to foster knowledge exchange, innovation, and capacity building. By engaging stakeholders from academia, industry, and policy, the project will explore cutting-edge energy storage technologies and their applications, contributing to Thailand’s decarbonization efforts and advancing its Sustainable Development Goals.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Hidden Narratives: Partnering with Generative AI to capture Youth Perspectives
descriptions: This study aims to uncover how the effects of social infrastructure flooding impacts the wellbeing vulnerabilities faced by youth—and youth opinions on nature-based adaptation strategies that can help to reduce these effects. The project will pilot an innovative, collaborative AI tool that empowers youth in Kenya to generate images that effectively communicate their vulnerabilities and perspectives on nature-based strategies to planners and community stakeholders.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Launching the Malawi Space Stars: A space technology awareness campaign to inspire the next generation of space leaders.
descriptions: In contemporary times, the notion of the new space economy has gained mome­ntum owing to the different ways that innovative space technologies show promise in re­shaping the socio-economic progress of a nation. For example, in case of Malawi a lot can be done regarding improvement of the areas such as education, disaster preparedness and planning for sustainable cities. Thus, we need to inspire the next generation of the young Malawians to take careers in space, science and technology so as to tap in the unseen potential. Nevertheless, a lot of Malawians have little or no knowledge of the advantages of space technology or available opportunities. To close this gap, we would like to introduce “The Malawi Space Stars” – a space tech awareness drive meant to inspire the youth to reach for the stars in Malawi. This campaign will target learners of all age levels from primary & secondary schools and universities. The campaign will utilize a variety of activities and outreach initiatives to engage Malawian youth, including: Educational workshops, Mentorship programs, Public outreach events, Social media campaigns, etc. These actions will probably increase space technology awareness in Malawi. Consequently, this will also increase interest of the learners for STEM. However, it is worth noting that our intended activities will demand international cooperation between Malawi and other developing African nations so as to set up a sustainable space technology ecosystem in Malawi. Truly, we are convinced that this campaign will make Malawi to be at the front of space in Africa and help expose the youth to space technology as well as mentor them. The partnership between Daka Space Technologies Ltd, the Malawi Government and international partners will bring out The Malawi Space Stars! The campaign is expected to launch on 8 December 2023 and will run for 12 Months.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Amplifying Impact: Engaging farmers and Showcasing Solutions for low cost greenhouse Climate-Resilient  (Vietnam)
descriptions:
Following the funding from Frontier seed funding with "Sustainable Farming with Low-Cost, Climate-Resilient Greenhouses in Vietnam and Africa" project, most of 
activities focus on designing and building sample products. With support from the Frontier Impact Grant, the team will open more workshops and promote the effectiveness of the project to more farmers. The grant will enable the team to create high-quality educational materials, develop communication strategies, organize dissemination activities, and host workshops. 

Amplify Outreach and Awareness: To communicate the outcomes and benefits of our low-cost greenhouse with climate-resilient agricultural practices to a broader audience, ensuring that stakeholders at all levels understand the potential for transformative change.
Encourage Adoption and Scale-Up: Showcasing successful case studies and proven techniques will inspire farmers, policymakers, and organizations to adopt low-cost greenhouses with climate-smart practices.
Promote Sustainable Change: After completing the project "Sustainable Farming with Low-Cost, Climate-Resilient Greenhouses in Vietnam and Africa" with a greenhouse sample product to combat climate change, the team will continue to promote the effectiveness of applying the model.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Integrating the WEFE Nexus into Engineering Education for Sustainable Development in Jordan
descriptions: This project is a transformative initiative designed to redefine engineering education in Jordan, guided by the principles of the Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystems (WEFE) Nexus. It aims to equip future engineers with the skills to address both global and local environmental challenges through an innovative curriculum that integrates advanced technologies, AI, and digital applications in construction, resource management, and infrastructure design. Additionally, the project will integrate gender and inclusion studies into the engineering curriculum to prepare students for diverse workplaces and ensure that solutions to WEFE challenges consider diverse perspectives and needs.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Bio-Based Design Network for regenerative built environment in emergent cities
descriptions:
"As the urban population in Asian cities is poised to surge in the coming years, resource-constrained emerging cities must adopt clever, adaptable, and low-resource-intensive solutions to enhance the quality of life for urban residents. Through this initiative, Utopia aims to delve into the potential of Bio-Based Design for constructing healthy, functional, and flexible built environments, focusing on emergent cities. Bio-based design, as a nascent research topic, enables broad exploration, experimentation, and co-creation of technologies and systemic practices with diverse groups of professionals. To foster the growth of bio-based design research and development, it is essential to establish global, regional, and local networks that serve as building blocks for innovation with a potential to reduce dependency on fossil fuels in the urban landscape.
Utopia aims to do so by bringing together experts, practitioners, creatives, and everyday users across two emergent cities – Dhaka and Kathmandu.
The goal is to discuss global practices, identify context-specific opportunities and challenges, and intensely explore the most compelling prospects during a 10-hour design program by groups of experts and practitioners from the two cities. The outcomes will be shared with a larger audience of regional and international participants, catalyzing broader discussions and experimentation.

The program design will employ future thinking and Human-Centered Design approaches enabling the participants to dissect the mindset around the deeper history of their cities leading to the present scenario and create future scenarios to identify crucial disrupters and actionable steps that can be taken in the present to shape a more sustainable future.

The network established will engage regional and international actors in the fields of design, regenerative design, built environment, urban studies, and future studies to share and build upon ideas. Utopia's approaches seek to provide a replicable template for collectively building and testing innovative ideas."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Bio-Based Design Network for regenerative built environment in emergent cities (Nepal)
descriptions:
The original grant focused on exploring Bio-Based Design for constructing healthy, functional, and flexible built environments, especially for emergent cities like Kathmandu where the urban population is increasing but the resources are constrained and the urban environment steadily diminishing. 

The first milestone of this project was the Global knowledge-based Webinar where practitioners from different regions shared knowledge and insights. Some key highlights were
The innovative technology being built in the West,
Indigenous knowledge is discounted by Eastern mindsets who deem RCC as the only modern and safe way of construction
The challenges of integrating sustainable materials and technology in the mainstream construction sector.
The insights were further enriched through conversations with different stakeholders in both the city. A stark difference in the adoption and endorsement of sustainable materials and technology between the two cities became even more apparent through these conversations.

The final milestone was the Futures-focused workshop conducted with a mixed group of participants from varied backgrounds based in Kathmandu with a low to medium knowledge of Bio-Based design. What was common among all the participants was curiosity and desire to learn more about Bio-Based design, and the acknowledgment of a needed change in Kathmandu’s urban environment.

With the Frontiers Impact Grant, more events will be hosted to engage a wider range of stakeholders, including informal and formal networks, through podcasts, speaker series and open-source futures toolkits.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: The future of GreenTower ESS – solar Energy Security as a Service for residential and business complexes
descriptions:
The proposed awardee excellence community event will be in the form of an in-person workshop with a maximum of 50 participants and 6 panelists followed by an online webinar to increase outreach to remote attendees.
The event has a number of aims namely to inform the participants regarding solar technologies, introduce a new energy as a service business model, interact with various professionals in the built environment, academia, industry as well as civil society and through beneficial communication to probe the advantages and disadvantages as well as sustainable benefits of various business models
Various activities will be included to ensure an interactive event. A total of 6 panelists from academia and industry will be introduced each with a relevant field of expertise with a number of interesting prizes to be won by participants.
The event will be structured over a 3-4 hour period which includes a tea break and light lunch. A mix of presentations, break out sessions, practical demonstrations and networking will aim to bring members of the community together from various backgrounds
The benefits will include a better understanding of solar technology and sustainability models along with an improved sense of community through networking. We will also be introducing the GreenTower online Solar technologies course with at least two lucky draw winners receiving free access to the course.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Increasing Resilience of Rural Healthcare: Climate-Friendly Energy & Digital Solutions (Kenya)
descriptions: Through interdisciplinary collaboration, this project aims to conduct a feasibility study on sustainable electrification of rural healthcare infrastructure in Siaya and Kisumu, Kenya. Expected results are the completion of two co-design workshops, a technical feasibility study, and a funding application to scale impactful solutions across the region. By enhancing energy access, this project aims to improve health outcomes and build a more resilient healthcare system for communities of Siaya and Kisumu.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Black Soldier Farming - a Scalable Business Case for Bangladesh Waste Workers
descriptions:
"Organic waste from kitchens, restaurants and markets currently ends up being dumped in the environment or at waste dumpsites where its decomposition generates methane gas – a potent greenhouse gas and a contributor to dumpsite fires which release black carbon and other airborne pollutants, and contaminating local waterbodies. 

This project will utilise this waste stream as a resource for the farming of Black Soldier Fly Larvae (BSFL) which is a high protein, high fat alternative to commercial animal feed for poultry and fish farming businesses in Bangladesh. This project will support waste and sanitation workers, who are already involved in waste management, to receive training and operate as entrepreneurs in BSFL farming, increasing their monthly earning potential ."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Designing Resilient Urban Mobility Systems for Climate Adaptation (Nepal)
descriptions: This project aims to explore pathways toward climate-resilient and inclusive urban mobility systems in South Asia by fostering discussions among urban planners, policymakers, technologists, researchers, and community representatives. This initiative will serve as a platform for dialogue, knowledge exchange, and collaborative exploration of strategies to integrate climate adaptation into urban transportation planning. Key activities will include stakeholder workshops in Nepal’s major urban regions, regional webinars featuring best practices from South Asia, and the development of policy briefs and research papers based on discussions. These outputs will highlight opportunities, challenges, and recommendations for fostering low-carbon, climate-resilient urban mobility systems that prioritise inclusivity and equity, particularly for vulnerable communities.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Empowering Communities with Circular Agriculture Literacy and Practices for Enhanced Food Security (Malaysia)
descriptions: The Frontiers Champion’s project focused on empowering communities with circular agriculture literacy and practices to enhance food safety. The team conducted all training activities in Malaysia and Indonesia as outlined in the project. Following the completion of these workshops, the project aims to evaluate the short-term impacts of our initiative and highlight its successes by creating a collection of case studies showcasing how participants have applied the lessons learned.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Building a sustainable network to formalise the informal sector on waste management for circularity  in East Africa
descriptions:
"African population is on the rise resulting in growth of production and consumption hence impacting the amount of resources used and waste generated and disposed. On the other hand, the rate of proper waste logistics and treatment is not growing at the same speed. Only limited categories of waste are handled in a proper circular manner due to inadequate recycling systems, infrastructure, policy and regulations and general awareness of the risks. The key categories of waste generated in African cities include organic waste, plastics, paper, metal, and electronic waste. 1.
Concerns have grown about the volume of plastic waste accumulating in cities, dumpsites, oceans and the natural environment. An estimated 25% of plastic waste is incinerated and 56% is disposed of in landfills.2
The systemic challenge and opportunity is the involvement of the informal sector. Informal waste and recycling operators are major contributors to the waste value chain and sustains livelihoods. In Kenya, the informal waste economy is a value chain of workers that contribute greatly to waste management, and many scavenge dumpsites to obtain recyclables.
Considering the challenges above, I would like to champion a stakeholders engagement platform to bring together the relevant actors in the waste sector with the aim of addressing the challenges and maximizing opportunities faced by informal waste management actors.
My championship would bring together a network from the national government, county government, private sector, development partners, education institutions, researchers and innovators, development partners and civil society to address the above-mentioned challenges and mainstream informal waste pickers into the formal sector."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Circular Hybrid Electrolyser Platform for Green Hydrogen Production from Food-Waste-Derived Bioethanol in Thailand
descriptions:
"Green hydrogen is a cornerstone of the global energy transition, yet conventional water electrolysis remains cost-prohibitive for many regions where infrastructure faces challenges like costs and capacity constraints, like Thailand, where this project will take place. This is largely due to the high electricity demand of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Hybrid electrolysers, which replace OER with selective oxidation of organic feedstocks, can reduce energy requirements by 50–70% while co-producing valuable chemicals. However, current systems are often tailored to specific, pre-sorted waste streams, making them poorly suited ot the diverse and mixed waste commonly enountered in Thailand and other emerging economies.

This project responds to the need in Thailand by developing a circular hybrid electrolyser platform designed for food-waste-derived bioethanol as a versatile and readily fermentable feedstock. Alcohol production via enzyme and yeast fermentation can utilise diverse sugar- and starch-containing waste without the need for strict sorting, enabling decentralised, low-cost feedstock generation. The project will integrate biological fermentation with electrochemical conversion to produce green hydrogen and green chemicals, while conducting supply chain mapping, techno-economic assessment, and life cycle analysis that will allow the team to understand Thailand’s relevant context including economic, infrastructural, and environmental conditions. This makes feedstock generation low‑cost, locally accessible, and adaptable to the specific rural and urban contexts locally and regionally.

The collaboration brings together expertise in electrocatalysis and energy conversion (Chulalongkorn University), biocatalysis (Northumbria University), membrane development (Chulalongkorn University), precision fermentation (BIOTEC, Thailand), business and supply chain analysis (Khon Kaen University), and energy device fabrication (Chulalongkorn University). Through this partnership, Thai institutions will benefit from strengthened technical capabilities in fermentation, membrane design, energy‑device fabrication, and sustainability assessment. The project will also build skills in emerging green‑hydrogen technologies, supporting workforce development and research leadership within Thailand.

The expected impact includes a functional prototype hybrid electrolyser, new insights into domestic food-waste-to-ethanol supply chains within Thailand and beyond, and comprehensive sustainability assessments. Environmental benefits for Thailand will include reduced greenhouse gas emissions and landfill burden. Social benefits will include wider access to decentralised clean energy and enhanced research skills. Economic benefits will include new value chains in waste valorisation, supporting Thailands transition toward a circular, low-carbon energy system"

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Scaling Affordable Prosthetic Solutions in Kenya and beyond (Kenya)
descriptions: This project aims to expand access to affordable and customized 3D-printed assistive devices in Kenya and beyond. By integrating prosthetic provision, local capacity building, and skills development, the initiative ensures a sustainable model for long-term impact. Using low-cost 3D printing, the team will co-create functional prosthetic solutions tailored to the needs of each beneficiary, empowering local communities with the necessary knowledge to continue production independently

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community-driven Journey Facilitation App for Public Transport: Co-creation of Services
descriptions: This project aims to improve the confidence of the community in public transport by innovating the community-operator interaction mechanism. The objectives are to develop a journey facilitation app (prototype) that can not only provide appropriate departure time based on estimated arrival time, but also correct feedback on service provision from users, and develop a forum that facilitates evidence-based and widely-accessible interactions for users and the operators to co-create service plans and environments, thereby installing confidence in PT among the community. As the main outputs, the team will create a prototype of the journey facilitation app as well as run an in-person workshop in the case study city (Penang, Malaysia) where users and the operator will develop PT service improvement plans based on evidence collected through the app. Learnings will be shared in Thailand, other Southeast Asian countries and beyond.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Navigating Conflict: A Comprehensive Analysis of Water Security and Food Security in Yemen
descriptions:
The ongoing conflict in Yemen has caused an unprecedented humanitarian crisis that has become the primary driver of water and food insecurity. Yemen has long struggled to meet its food needs, producing only ten per cent of its requirements while facing an acute water scarcity, resulting in the spread of water-borne illnesses and diseases owing to a lack of safe and sufficient drinking water and inadequate sanitation.

The project aims to investigate the impact of Yemen's conflict on water and food security, particularly in terms of availability, accessibility, affordability, and quality. By analyzing the situation before and after the war, the project seeks to shed light on the nexus between conflict and water and food security and what are the repercussions on Yemen in terms of resource security and the development of internal conflicts.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: A Chatbot to Enhance Adolescent Mental Health Wellness in Kenya
descriptions: Mental health issues are a growing concern worldwide, and Kenya is no exception. One study estimated that 1 in 8 adolescents met the criteria for a mental disorder in Kenya. Access to mental health services is often limited, especially in resource-constrained settings. The study findings and restricted access to services indicate a need for a digital mental wellness intervention. This project, "Imarisha Afya ya Akili" (Enhance Mental Wellness), aims from a human-centred design methodology to improve mental well-being in Kenya by providing accessible and culturally relevant adolescent-targeted mental wellness support through a social media-based digital intervention. The web-based social media intervention “Dəˈskəs” is a co-designed digital intervention that offers adolescents a “safe” space to connect with their peers and access health information. “Dəˈskəs” was developed by the lead applicant during his postdoc fellowship. The project aims to focus on self-care, stress management, wellness, and peer learning, leveraging the widespread use of social media in Kenya. By incorporating culturally relevant content and an adolescent-designed and developed social media platform, the project aims to meet adolescent users’ needs and expectations when accessing social media-based digital health interventions and reach a large and diverse population. The expected results include: 1) increased awareness and understanding of mental health issues. 2) improved access to mental health support; enhanced self-care and stress management skills 3) increased social support and reduced feelings of isolation; empowered adolescents and communities to take control of their mental well-being. The project team comprises a human-centred design researcher, a human-centred design and digital health researcher, a clinical psychologist, and a software developer. Collaboration with Kenyan adolescent users will ensure that the co-designed intervention is tailored to the specific needs and context of the Kenyan adolescent population. This innovative approach has the potential to contribute to improving mental outcomes among adolescents in Kenya

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Eco-friendly Decorative Tiles from Textile Waste, Incorporating Sustainable Binders and Assessment of the Environmental Impact
descriptions:
"The global textile industry generates over 92 million tonnes of solid waste annually and currently ranks as the 2nd most polluting industry after oil. In developing countries, including Tanzania, this problem is intensified by the importation of second-hand clothing and the lack of structured waste management systems. 

The proposed project aims to address these challenges by transforming textile waste, currently disposed of through landfill or incineration, into value-added products for use as decorative tiles. This project builds on the successful development of prototype tiles from recycled textile waste combined with synthetic binders during Phase I at the University of Dar es Salaam in Tanzania. The current phase proposes a shift from synthetic binders to eco-friendly binders, including bio-based resins such as lignin, natural polymers like chitosan, and recycled materials, especially those derived from PET waste. Through this phase, optimal combinations of textile waste with natural or bio-based binders will be developed, ensuring that both performance and aesthetic properties are maintained."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Extending Dialogue on Transport Systems Curricula for Africa
descriptions: The main objective of this project is to operationalise  an Africa-wide network of transport infrastructure experts that will improve the sector's curricula in various regions of the continent, depending on emerging technologies and needs for resilient transport infrastructure. Based on the initial curriculum developed in this program, this project aims to establish a transport systems engineering program with input from as many regions of Africa as possible.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Data Assessment Methodology of Kenya WASH Programme, Analysing WEFE Impacts
descriptions:
In the drought-stricken landscapes of Southeast Kenya, communities face escalating challenges regarding access to clean water and food security, compelling women and girls to undertake perilous 6–12-hour daily journeys for water. This project proposes a transformative approach to Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) through a detailed analysis of sand dam projects and associated community trainings, emphasising their multifaceted impacts on Water, Energy, Food, and the Environment (WEFE).

Previous works show that sand dam programmes provide the capability to store up to 40 million litres of clean water, deliver community-focused training and provide food security. They also directly improve the biodiversity and improve the quality of life of communities in the surrounding area.

Our objective is twofold: in the short-term, to generate a comprehensive data-driven baseline highlighting the immediate benefits of sand dams. The impact of WASH projects on climate, such as carbon credit, carbon footprint, and life-cycle assessments, has not been quantified, despite their positive impact on both the environment and society.

Our second objective, therefore, is long-term, to leverage this evidence, including measurable climate impacts, to build a compelling investment model for WASH initiatives.

By highlighting the critical intersection of sustainability, community empowerment, and climate resilience, we aim to unlock new funding streams, including climate finance, and catalyse a paradigm shift in addressing water scarcity.

The project addresses relevant SDGs at its core, primarily that of SDG 6, Clean Water and Sanitation, as well as SDG 3: Good Health and Well-Being, SDG 5: Gender Equality and SDG 4: Quality Education, illustrating the interconnected nature of these goals.

The activities delivered in this project ensure women are physically represented, actively involved and in leadership positions during implementation, gender equality is very much included in all activities.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: EndoConnect Hub for Bridging Gaps and Building Networks for Endometriosis Support in East Africa
descriptions: EndoConnect Hub is a pioneering initiative designed to revolutionise support for women with endometriosis in East Africa, starting in Uganda. This project aims to build a robust digital and community network using SMS, WhatsApp, and AI technologies to connect women, referred to as endometriosis warriors, with essential resources, expert care, and peer support. It addresses inefficiencies in existing support group communications, such as the repetitive sharing of information among over 100 members, offering a streamlined and accessible solution.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: RESCUE: Recovery for Equitable Support in Climate Undermined Environments
descriptions: The project aims to enhance disaster risk management (DRM) in vulnerable informal settlements by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and remote sensing (RS) technologies. It focuses on understanding recovery processes in marginalized communities affected by Brazil’s 2019 floods and India’s 2024 monsoon floods through targeted data collection and stakeholder workshops.  Expected outcomes include an open-access, centralised database for collected data and a peer-reviewed publication detailing methodologies for integrating DRM, AI, and RS, serving as the foundation for a larger implementation and scalability proposal.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Coevolving Sustainable Resilient Groundwater Systems in Uganda
descriptions:
The aim of the project is to bring together people who are interested in creating a sustainable resilient groundwater system but would not usually have a chance to meet or discuss this mutual aim in their everyday activities. Some of these people may even hold adversarial views of each other based on policies that have been implemented or held responsible for water access outcomes. These people would include academics, professionals, policy makers, technicians, funders, and community members who are borehole users. The core academic team will come from both the University College London (UCL) and Makerere University. The other participants will be from Uganda and the Kyoga catchment.

The main activity will be a three-day workshop. The first day will build trust amongst participants through introductory activities and a borehole infrastructure safari where we will visit operational and non-operational boreholes, an installation site, and a prospective site. The second day will put together what people’s perspectives are of the groundwater system and demonstrate how different parts of the system affect one another. We will also explore the enablers and prohibitors to change. The third day will be an imaginative day where people can play with the system creating new sustainable resilient groundwater systems, identifying all the ways the existing system would need to change, what would need to be in place to facilitate this to occur, evaluating the feasibility of each proposal, and committing to an action.

The benefit of the workshop is that each participant would gain new knowledge about the groundwater system by sharing their knowledge with other participants. Each person would learn the constraints and possibilities open to each role and discover how these could be mutually beneficial. This will increase the capacity for a sustainable resilient groundwater system to be developed in the future.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Science, Technology, and Sustainable Cities Innovation Network in Southeast Asia (STSCIN)
descriptions:
The Science, Technology, and Sustainable Cities Innovation Network in Southeast Asia (STSCIN) is a transformative initiative building upon the success of the existing AISC network. The project aims to unite experts in science, technology, and innovation to strengthen the capacity of Southeast Asian nations in addressing pressing issues linked with Sustainable Development Goal 11 (SDG11). With 50% of the South-East Asian population residing in urban areas, STSCIN targets challenges related to inclusiveness, environmental sustainability, and health. STSCIN is strategically structured into two interlinked tracks: 1) cooperation in science and technology, and 2) innovation in smart sustainable cities.

Participants will gain invaluable insights through pilot city studies and technical knowledge exchange, focusing on artificial intelligence, robotics, cloud computing, agri-tech, energy modeling, and 6G for sustainable cities. The network provides a platform for professionals to socialize new ideas, fostering a collaborative environment for innovation. The project includes a series of six (6) technical webinars aligned with sustainable cities. Network members attending these webinars will qualify to participate in the Sustainable City Innovation Challenge, where selected participants will highlight research concepts demonstrating real-world applications or producing data beneficial in Southeast Asia. This challenge aims to showcase practical solutions and data-driven insights to address urban challenges in the region.

STSCIN will select and cover all travel expenses for qualifying participants attending the workshop in Penang, Malaysia. The project envisions becoming a catalyst for transformative changes, cultivating a robust regional network that leverages science, technology, and innovation to advance smart and sustainable urban development in Southeast Asia. Through collaborative efforts, the network seeks to contribute significantly to the achievement of SDG11 and foster a resilient and inclusive future for the region.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: EdCon2023- Conference on Innovative Education Solutions for Sustainable Development in Africa (Sierra Leone)
descriptions:
The Frontiers Impact Grant will amplify the impact and reach of EdCon2023 by creating resources that extend the discussion, learnings, and solutions derived from the event to a wider audience. EdCon2023 provided a unique platform for educators, policymakers, and innovators to address critical issues in African education, such as curriculum reform and girl-child education. 

With the Frontiers Impact Grant, our primary objective is to amplify the impact of EdCon2023 by effectively communicating its key outcomes, insights, and solutions to a broader audience. Through strategic dissemination, we aim to foster deeper engagement, spark meaningful conversations, and inspire actionable steps toward addressing educational challenges in Africa.

We plan to achieve this through two key approaches:

Social Media Reels: We will create 20 engaging, easily digestible short videos highlighting key discussions, solutions, and insights from EdCon2023. These reels, drawn from panel discussions, interactive sessions, and interviews, will be shared on platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube Shorts to reach diverse audiences, especially youth and educators.

Podcasts: We will produce two video and audio podcast episodes featuring Sierra-Leone Education Stakeholders &key speakers from EdCon2023. These episodes will delve deeper into critical themes such as curriculum reform for African education and challenges and opportunities in girl-child education. Each podcast will generate additional content, including articles, quote cards, and short clips for broader distribution.

By leveraging digital platforms, we aim to reach over 50,000 viewers, expand awareness, and ensure that the outcomes of EdCon2023 continue to influence stakeholders, including educators, policymakers, and advocates, for sustainable educational development in Africa.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Piezoelectric & low-cost Nano Coating on to Solar Panels to sustain efficiency
descriptions: The proposed project seeks to revolutionize solar panel cleaning through the development, deployment of two merged technologies Nanocoating and Piezoelectric films for self-cleaning purposes. By harnessing the unique properties of Piezoelectric materials, our system will induce controlled vibrations to effectively remove dust particles from solar panels, eliminating the need for water entirely, the nanocoating part will reduce water droplets from sticking to the surface creating a muddy dust. This innovative approach not only addresses environmental concerns associated with water usage but also enhances the efficiency and longevity of solar panels. Furthermore, the versatility of Piezoelectric technology extends beyond solar panel applications, offering potential solutions for cleaning automotive and radar camera’s and mitigating dust accumulation on the solar panels of space exploration Rovers. Through interdisciplinary science and engineering collaboration and innovation, this project endeavors to advance sustainable infrastructure initially in Jordan, while also contributing to global efforts in renewable energy development.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Social Entrepreneurship as a path to Sustainable and Equitable Development in Sierra Leone
descriptions: This project aims to use Social Entrepreneurship as a mechanism to catalyse Sustainable and Equitable Development in Sierra Leone via two main project pillars - Capacity Building and Ecosystem Building in the domain of Social Entrepreneurship. Through the delivery of a free virtual Social Entrepreneurship Training course, the project will build the capacity of young people in Sierra Leone to become social entrepreneurs and start their own social ventures (proposed as an alternative path to livelihoods generation, given the lack of jobs and high rates of youth unemployment in the country) - thus, addressing SDG 8 "Decent Work and Economic Growth". These young social entrepreneurs will in turn be able to create more jobs for others, while addressing various social and/or environmental problems faced by the country (arising due to high rates of multidimensional poverty), through the creation of innovative and financially sustainable social ventures - in turn, addressing SDG 1 "No Poverty" and SDG 10 "Reduced Inequalities". Additionally, through a combination of virtual community-building initiatives and an in-person network-building event in Freetown, the project aims to create a systemic business mindset shift in Sierra Leone by bringing together various innovation ecosystem stakeholders (students, social entrepreneurs, universities, impact investors, philanthropists, government, corporates, NGOs and enterprise support organisations such as incubators/accelerators) to harness the country's collective social innovation potential - thus, contributing to the development of the nascent social entrepreneurship ecosystem in Sierra Leone and in turn, addressing SDG 9 "Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure". In sum, through Capacity Building and Ecosystem Building activities, this project will catalyse Social Entrepreneurship as a path to Sustainable and Equitable Development in Sierra Leone.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Leveraging digital tools to visualize climate impacts on the everyday city (Nepal)
descriptions: The project, funded through seed funding, aimed to address the critical gap in understanding hyperlocal climate impacts and the lack of accessible tools for visualising these insights. The primary purpose was to empower communities and decision-makers with inclusive, data-driven narratives to foster informed urban planning and sustainable resilience. With the Frontiers Impact Grant, the team aims to amplify these achievements, identify best practices, and advocate for the adoption of digital tools in city planning. Additionally, the team plans to transform the High Fidelity Prototype into a fully functional website. This upgrade will serve as a platform for disseminating findings to a broader audience, ensuring research is not only accessible but also contributes to an ongoing, public dialogue on sustainable urban development.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Empowering Tech: Bridging Gender Gaps through Financial and Digital Literacy in Uganda and beyond
descriptions: This proposal addresses the empowerment of women through financial and digital literacy in Uganda alongside Kenya, Rwanda and Tanzania, aligning with the UK Government's Gender Equality in Research and Innovation Policy and the Sustainable Development Goal 5 (SDG 5) objectives. Collaborating with The Royal Academy of Engineering and leveraging the Frontiers Champions initiative, the project aims to contribute to an inclusive economy and sustainable solutions. As an academician and Frontier Champion, the Project identifies a gap in women's information technology education, particularly in basic financial and business skills, hindering their potential despite innovating impactful technologies. The proposed approach integrates Functional Adult Literacy (FAL), Basic Computing for Adults (BCFA), and Business Skills Training (BST) to bridge this gap and positively impact gender equity hence ensuring inclusivity and addressing unique challenges faced by women in technology. The commitment to measuring outcomes through a gender lens, reporting to Frontier Champions, and actively monitoring and evaluating the project's lifecycle ensures accountability and effectiveness in promoting gender equality and empowerment. In Summary, this project not only addresses the gender gap in technology education but also contributes to a future where women actively participate in shaping the digital landscape, fostering an inclusive and diverse society in line with SDG 5.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Thailand's Energy Transition: Unveiling the Missing Puzzle Piece
descriptions: Energy transition is a global imperative, and Thailand stands at a critical juncture in this transformative journey. With ambitious sustainability goals and growing energy demands, the nation's commitment to a greener future is clear. However, navigating the complexities of such a profound shift requires nuanced understanding of the challenges and opportunities unique to Thailand's context. Our project, "Thailand's Energy Transition: Unveiling the Missing Puzzle Piece” emerges as a strategic response to this imperative, designed to propel Thailand towards its carbon neutrality aspirations by 2050. Through a series of targeted activities, including webinars, stakeholder workshops, design thinking sessions, and a cross-country workshop in the UK, our project addresses the multifaceted dimensions of energy transition. The webinars, featuring experts from diverse fields, aim to illuminate the path forward by sharing global best practices and insights tailored to Thailand's needs. Stakeholder workshops offer collaborative space for policymakers, industry leaders, and researchers to coalesce around innovative strategies, fostering a unified vision for sustainable energy practices. In tandem, design thinking workshops engage students—future leaders and change-makers—in exploring the intricate facets of Thailand's energy landscape. This not only cultivates innovative thinking but also ensures a legacy of sustainable practices carried forward by the next generation. At the project's apex lies the cross-country workshop in the UK, where insights from Thailand are shared and compared with international best practices. This workshop not only contributes to SDG 13 but also serves as a hub for cross-border collaboration, addressing global challenges and promoting shared solutions. In essence, this project is positioned as a catalyst for positive change, untangling complexities of Thailand's energy transition and contributing to a more sustainable global energy landscape. The multidisciplinary approach, inclusive practices, and international collaboration embedded in the project underscore its significance in advancing the goals of sustainable development and climate action.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Reducing Mobile Money Fraud in Malawi
descriptions:
This grant will enable the team to showcase lessons learned from the pilot project in rural Malawi. It will also help establish relationships with key stakeholders to develop new innovative solutions to combat mobile money fraud across Africa.
To communicate and disseminate this impact effectively, the team will develop engaging videos and infographics featuring a stakeholder interview series. The team will also co-host a session with GSMA at the Mobile World Congress Kigali 2025 (October) during the Mobile for Development event.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Turning Food Waste into Renewable Energy: A Sustainable Community-Scale Solution
descriptions:
"In Malaysia, approximately 8.3 million metric tons of food waste are generated annually,  while Thailand produces around 9.7 million metric tons. A significant portion of this waste is oily in nature, which poses challenges for conventional biogas systems. These existing systems are often large in scale, expensive to build, and unsuitable for small businesses or community-level use. 

This project brings together researchers from Malaysia, Thailand, and the UK to carry out laboratory studies on oily food waste to generate essential technical data for designing a modular, small-scale biogas unit tailored for oily food waste. This unit will be decentralised and low-cost, allowing communities and small enterprises to turn waste into clean energy while creating new income opportunities. It is projected to improve methane yield by up to 20% compared to untreated oily substrates, with initial deployment targeting two community-scale units and diverting over 100 tons of food waste annually."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Developing a Feasibility Framework for MedTech in Low-Resource Settings: NeoNest Uganda
descriptions: This project will develop and test a lean feasibility assessment framework tailored for MedTech innovators in Low- and Middle-Income Countries. The framework will offer a structured yet adaptable approach to pre-market evaluation, ensuring effective adoption, scalability, and integration into resource-limited healthcare systems. To validate the framework, the team will apply it to NeoNest, a low-cost neonatal transport incubator developed by Makerere University and Duke University to prevent neonatal hypothermia during emergency referrals.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Affordable and sustainable green homes for underprivileged people in Africa
descriptions:
The Frontiers seed funding project was dedicated to addressing the pressing issue of affordable housing in Sub-Saharan Africa through innovative construction technologies and sustainable practices. During the symposium held in May 2024, the team gathered valuable insights, feedback, and information from various stakeholders, which will be compiled into a comprehensive impact report focused on the African region under this project.

This dual-format publication—digital and physical—will disseminate the findings regarding the suitability and feasibility of different construction methodologies to a broad audience, including industry professionals, community members, and other key stakeholders in Sub-Saharan Africa. 

Moreover, our report will be shared with universities, researchers, and government officials, ensuring that the insights and recommendations can inform the formulation of effective affordable housing policies on a larger scale. Additionally, microfinance institutions, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and gender-focused initiatives in Africa will find our findings valuable for their ongoing work in promoting sustainable development and enhancing access to housing for underserved populations.

By fostering collaboration and providing actionable insights, our project aims to contribute significantly to the ongoing efforts to create a more sustainable and equitable housing landscape in Sub-Saharan Africa.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Empowering Communities with Circular Agriculture Literacy and Practices for Enhanced Food Security
descriptions: This project focuses on addressing the challenges posed by fluctuating food costs and the protection of vulnerable communities through the adoption of circular agriculture practices and localized agricultural development. The primary goal is to empower urban and rural communities with the knowledge and skills necessary for circular agriculture, with the active involvement of various stakeholders, including industry experts, academics, government officials, and community representatives. The project will create training materials and organize workshops in both urban Kuala Lumpur and rural Kedah. These workshops will educate participants on circular practices, with a specific focus on cultivating microalgae and black soldier fly (BSF) and converting them into alternative animal feeds and fertilizers. After training, participants will receive support and guidance to establish their microalgae and BSF cultivation systems, ensuring the successful integration of circular agriculture practices into their existing farming routines. To incentivize adoption, a competition will be held to recognize those who achieve the best yields and utilization of microalgae and BSF in their farming activities. An online webinar will disseminate circular agriculture concepts to the wider public, sharing the successes and experiences of both communities and professional practitioners. A dedicated project website will provide training materials, progress updates, photos, and reflections, serving as a platform for information exchange between communities and the public. Additionally, the project will facilitate knowledge exchange by organizing a site visit to community greenhouse farming in Aceh, Indonesia, where the experiences of implementing circular agriculture practices in Malaysia will be shared, promoting their adoption in the Aceh community. In summary, this project's overarching aim is to enhance food security, protect communities from food price fluctuations, and contribute to sustainable development by promoting the widespread adoption of circular agriculture practices.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Leveraging Digital Health Platforms to Improve Access to Quality Care and Enhance Treatment Adherence in Underserved Communities in Yemen
descriptions:
This project aims to leverage digital health platforms to enhance access to quality healthcare and support treatment adherence in underserved communities. The initiative will focus on raising awareness and education through webinars and workshops, highlighting the transformative potential of digital health technologies. It will also emphasise some i-Health applications such as telemedicine, health data management, and remote consultations to demonstrate how these tools can address healthcare challenges. The project will also inspire innovation through competitions, encouraging professionals and community health workers to develop creative digital health solutions tailored to their communities, with a focus on gender equality and addressing gender-specific healthcare challenges.

Expected outcomes include increased awareness and understanding of digital health solutions, improved skills in utilizing these tools, enhanced communication between patients and healthcare providers, and the creation of innovative, community-centred solutions. The project will ultimately contribute to reducing healthcare disparities, improving health equity, and empowering underserved communities to achieve better healthcare outcomes.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Golden Thread to Sustainability, Inclusivity, Affordability and Futureproofing in the Global South through Innovative Advancements in Net-Positive Hou
descriptions:
The Global South, which hosts most of the world’s population, is unequivocally more vulnerable to climate change, owing to widespread poverty, income inequality and its heavy dependence on climate-sensitive sectors. Considering that Carbon dioxide (CO2) is the main greenhouse gas emitted by human activities, the South has contributed significantly to global emissions in the past three decades, accounting for approximately 63% of today's total Greenhouse Gas (GHGs) emissions. While existing efforts are mainly focused on achieving net zero carbon emissions, this project goes beyond the current practices by introducing an integrative and transformative approach: Sustainable, Innovative, Affordable and Net-Positive housing (SIAH-NP). SIAH-NP addresses housing inefficiencies and aligns with the 2050 carbon neutrality target, striving to redefine housing into innovative hubs able of generating greater environmental and socio-economic values than they consume.
Combining Modern Methods of Design and Construction (MDMC), Circular Economy (CE) principles, and Smart Decentralised Systems (SDS), SIAH-NP aims to redefine the new generation of housing, minimising its environmental footprint, fostering resilience and contributing to carbon neutrality, directly impacting the path to a sustainable future in the Global South and beyond. SIAH-NP covers the conceptualisation, detailed design and sustainability study based on the climatic conditions and socio-economic situations of two representative countries in the Global South: Jordan and South Africa. Research findings are expected to provide invaluable information for housing stakeholders, leading the sector towards sustainability, inclusiveness, affordability and futureproofing. A bottom-up approach is therefore essential to achieve the proposed objectives. The research outlines a convincing pathway for transforming housing into models of sustainable progress, aiming to mitigate the looming threat of housing emissions and fostering a net-positive impact on social, environmental, and economic aspects, particularly in food, water, and energy and consequently the quality of life in the Global South.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Solutions for Enhancing Flooding Resilience of Coastal Roads in Indonesia
descriptions: The purpose of this project is to develop sustainable solutions for enhancing the flooding resilience of coastal roads in Indonesia. This study will investigate the characteristics of local floods to identify a vulnerable coastal road section in Banda Aceh (a coastal city that is prone to flooding) for a case study and assess the flooding impacts on coastal roads to understand the flood-related road distresses and the community accessibility. Samples of existing local paving materials will be secured for laboratory tests. Their properties and climate resilience will be improved through novel nature-based methods.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Comprehensive Assessment of WASH Programme, Focusing on WEFE Impacts (Kenya)
descriptions:
This dissemination project will highlight the positive impact of the seed funding grant and showcase the project’s key findings. The seed funding project is a detailed analysis of the impact of sand dams in Kenya and associated community training, which has a clear impact on WEFE.

This dissemination will highlight the positive impact of the grant, showcasing the project’s key findings. The team will produce: a visual resource (infographic); a short film which highlights the main findings; dedicate a section of the Just a Drop website for the findings; comprehensive social media, with a small budget to push posts to relevant accounts; organise and online webinar / workshop; and produce a full, designed report.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Towards Spatial-Environmental Justice: Creating and Nurturing Transnational Climate-Aware Knowledge Networks
descriptions:
"This proposal aims to build, expand, and nurture transnational climate-aware knowledge networks across the Indian subcontinent in India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Bhutan. Knowledge networks are constellations of people and teams across boundaries (e.g., spatial, disciplinary) to develop, distribute, combine, and apply collective knowledge to address a problem. Steered by the Champion, the transnational networks will be created over 10-12 months via virtual engagement and an in-person 2-day charrette in India. Our recent work at the intersection of a) unprecedented urbanization, attendant fragmentation of city ecologies and biodiversity loss; b) changing climates and its manifestation in extreme events; and, c) the cumulative disproportionate impact on the poor and marginalized has reiterated the need for collaborative working to achieve spatial and environmental justice in the burgeoning global South city. It calls for an adaptation of the existing centralized, standardized and siloed modes to adopt context-specific, flexible, dynamic and iterative modes of engagement that transcend the traditional city-stakeholders - urban development departments, architects, planners – and scales.

The project will mobilize stakeholders across diverse domains, spatialities, scales and contexts - working at various points on the continuum between grass-roots interventions on one hand and plan and policy on the other. The objective is two-pronged: moving beyond mere information sharing to create pipelines for knowledge creation and disseminate it to enhance capacities of young professionals. Sharing of case studies, attendant methods and approaches, ensuing challenges (including those of scale and replication), needs and aspirations will be encouraged. The Urban Lab will aim to provide a space for collaboration between local and transnational stakeholders, using the knowledge to foster a deeper understanding of collaborative mode of problem framing and resolutions facilitating environmental and spatial justice for marginalized communities. The Champion will leverage her prior experience in intersectional collaboration to curate conversations."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Optimization of Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) for Enhanced WEFE Nexus Performance
descriptions:
Jordan faces significant challenges related to water scarcity and is considered one of the most water-scarce countries in the world. This would have adverse impacts of climate change on agriculture, leading to heightened concerns about food security. To address these challenges, there is a growing need to enhance food security at the national level while optimizing resource use and adapting to climate change impacts. Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA), supported by photovoltaics (PV) and hydroponic systems, presents promising opportunities to improve irrigation water efficiency and maximize crop yields, facilitating the transition to climate-resilient agriculture, while promoting continued growth and creating green jobs.
This proposed project matches the WEFE Nexus approach by minimizing irrigation water and utilizing a sustainable energy source for producing agricultural crops through a climate-resilient agriculture technique.

The proposed project aims to further advance CEA and hydroponics in Jordan by:
1. Providing interactive and accessible cultivation information to consultancy providers and stakeholders through the development of a mobile application.
2. Developing an autonomous agricultural unit controlled by IoT technology to optimize resource use and crop production.
3. Conducting awareness sessions and training seminars on climate-resilient agriculture.
4. Strengthening collaboration between the RSS and UK universities to promote knowledge exchange.
5. Disseminating project findings through scientific publications.
Through these efforts, the project seeks to design a modern, marketable agricultural unit capable of producing high-quality crops, particularly in urban areas, thereby contributing to enhanced food security and climate resilience in Jordan, applicable to other countries such as Egypt.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Revolutionise Engineering: Vision infinity student vanguard
descriptions:
"One of the challenges facing businesses in kenya is finding qualified workers with specialist IT skills. The skills shortage is particularly acute in the areas of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technologies such AI, Data Science, Computer Vision, Virtual reality, Augmented Reality, Blockchain, Space Tech and others. To address this skills shortage and fortify the local IT sector, my project seeks collaboration with the Frontiers community of experts. The initiative aims to establish and execute a program called ""Revolutionize Engineering"" enabling Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) as well as university students in Kenya to acquire expertise in 4IR technologies through a series of hackathons and makerthons.
Revolutionize Engineering is a transformative one-year project, with a goal of establishing a community of 10,000 passionate engineering students in Africa, particularly in Kenya, focusing on emerging Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technologies. The project team has developed a sustainable, long-term training strategy that focuses on building the practical skills needed in the IT sector. The training, hackathons and Makerthons are industry-led and open to Kenyan university and TVET students.

In strategic collaboration with companies in the emerging tech sector, the project creates pathways for students to access job opportunities, allowing them to apply their skills to tackle some of the world's most challenging problems.

Beyond skill development and career support, Revolutionize Engineering advocates for the pivotal role of emerging technologies in Africa's future, recognizing the continent's critical juncture in navigating the Fourth Industrial Revolution."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Innovative Smart and Sustainable Agriculture Network: Climate Change Adaptation and Connecting Farmers from Asia to Africa
descriptions: This project aims to establish a robust and inclusive network for smart and sustainable agriculture, focusing on innovation and climate change adaptation. By connecting farmers across Asia and Africa, the initiative seeks to foster knowledge exchange, technology transfer, and collaborative problem-solving. The network will prioritize sustainable practices that enhance agricultural productivity, resilience, and environmental stewardship while addressing region-specific challenges posed by climate change. Ultimately, the project aspires to empower farmers, advance sustainable agriculture, and contribute to global efforts in achieving resilience and sustainability in the face of climate change.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Higher Education Partnerships in sub-Saharan Africa Cohort Support Spend 23-25
Higher Education Partnerships in sub-Saharan Africa Cohort Support Spend 24-25
descriptions: Spend on shared activities for Higher Education Partnerships in sub-Saharan Africa award holders

Spend on shared activities for Higher Education Partnerships in sub-Saharan Africa award holders, largely universities in Africa to enable and support them produce graduates fit for employment in their local communities.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Enhancing engineering education in sub-Saharan Africa through a research and innovation pipeline
descriptions:
In response to the pressing need for skilled engineers capable of addressing complex challenges in Sub-Saharan Africa, this project aims to establish a Research and Innovation Pipeline within universities across the region. The initiative seeks to instill a culture of research, critical thinking, and collaboration among undergraduate and postgraduate students. By providing specialized training, mentorship, and access to industry partnerships, the project aspires to nurture the next generation of skilled researchers and professionals equipped to tackle national and regional challenges.
Development Challenge Addressed: The project addresses the critical need for a well-trained and innovative engineering workforce in Sub-Saharan Africa. The region faces challenges in areas such as infrastructure development, renewable energy, and sustainable technologies. The shortage of skilled engineers hinders progress in these key sectors. This project directly confronts this issue by building research capacities, fostering innovation, and creating avenues for collaboration between universities and industry partners.
Alignment with HEP SSA Programme Objectives: The project aligns seamlessly with the objectives of the HEP SSA programme, which aims to enhance higher education for sustainable socio-economic development in Sub-Saharan Africa.
