By establishing a Research and Innovation Pipeline, the project contributes to:
1. Capacity Building: Providing specialized training programs and mentorship opportunities enhances the research capacities of students.
2. Innovation and Entrepreneurship: By facilitating innovation challenges and competitions, the project encourages students to develop practical solutions, fostering an entrepreneurial spirit among the next generation of engineers.
3. Industry-Academia Collaboration: The establishment of partnerships with industry stakeholders

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Catalysing Sustainable Futures in Africa: Transforming Engineering and Built Environment Higher Education to Bridge Knowledge and Technological Innova
descriptions:
The Southern African region faces numerous pressing development challenges, including substantial infrastructure deficits, limited access to clean water and sanitation, a significant backlog in affordable housing, an energy crisis, and the world's highest unemployment rate. The region lacks critical knowledge and expertise in SD and TIs to address these urgent issues. This gap, particularly pronounced in the Engineering and Built Environment Professions (EBEPs), is of profound importance for Southern Africa's sustainable future and its citizens' overall quality of life.

To bridge this knowledge gap, the Higher Education for Sustainable Development (HESD) approach will be leveraged, emphasising the pivotal role played by universities and professional bodies in nurturing a skilled workforce for the industry and who can address multifaceted modern societal challenges. Consequently, the emerging social, economic, and environmental imperatives are succinctly captured in the targets and benchmarks outlined by the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and the Africa 2063 Agenda.

To realise these SDG targets and local objectives, advocacy is made for the adoption of the Quintuple Helix Model of Innovation (5HIM), which suggests the deployment of a collaborative framework which encompasses five ’helices’ or subsystems in the realm of HESD: academia, industry, policymakers, civil society and the environment. The synergy of efforts among the stakeholders who represent these ecosystems, is envisioned to drive sustainable development through adoption of TIs, fostering innovation and enhancement of knowledge and skills of Southern African EBE graduates and professionals thus equipping them to address the complex challenges faced by the Southern African societies.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: An Industry based Approach to Review Agricultural Engineering Curriculum and Develop Capacity of Undergraduates and Early Career Academics of Institut
descriptions: The employment landscape is changing because of the fourth industrial revolution and in the recent years it has become clear that the university-industry link is very important. According to Statistics South Africa, the main reason for a high unemployment rate (40.3%) of young people between the age of 15-24 is the inability to find jobs that suit the university training and skill set. This provides clarity that universities' role in meeting industry needs is behind, hence the need to review the Agricultural Engineering curriculum. Agriculture remains the key industry to develop in SSA countries. Training highly relevant skilled individuals has economic benefits because most of the economically beneficial technology are produced directly or indirectly by universities. Reforming and modernising the curriculum requires a collaborative effort to ensure that there are sufficient progression routes and a suitable balance between the production of engineers, technologists, and technicians, with a current specific focus on developing the number and capacity of engineering technologists and technicians (PASAE report). To meet the student demand for relevant knowledge, the staff in the respective institutions should have sufficient practical training, that is supported by ECSA registration. Therefore, this project intends to meet the HEP SSA programme objective through enhancing the engineering capacity by developing the agricultural curricula in the institutions that offer agricultural engineering degrees as well as introduce practice workshops for students to learn from industry the skills that are missing when they graduate.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Innovation and Digitalisation pathways for a more affordable housing in Sub-Saharan Africa
descriptions:
Global demand for affordable housing is on the rise due to rapid urbanization, economic challenges, high unemployment, poverty, and the effect of climate change. In the era of Anthropocene, the record of flooding, subsidence is more frequent, which impacts the rapid increases in human population and results in political unrest. These problems are much more evident and have a wider spatial exposure, in the countries of sub-Saharan Africa where there is growing sustained demand for low-cost or affordable housing. However, low-quality workmanship, sub-optimal construction methods, ineffective collaboration, poor coordination, little communication result in delays affecting the project delivery time. Energy waste, problems with electrification, inefficient water use, high carbon footprints, unsustainable practices in housing delivery and construction technologies, are contributing into a growing housing backlog.

Cloud-Based Building Information Modelling, 3D-Printing, modular construction are widely recognised technologies, that can enhance, the rate of delivering of affordable houses. Training and associated cost, along with scepticism from industry professionals suggest that further research can be undertaken to investigate the impact of innovation and digitisation in the increase of construction delivery.

The project is proposing a triangulation of activities to introduce civil engineering and built environment graduates to innovation and digital methods, which enhance engineering capacity in sub-Saharan Africa by improving the knowledge, skills, and employability of engineering graduates. The project aims to build on the research and innovation capacity of higher education institutions in sub-Saharan Africa and stimulate ties with the industry sector to increase the scale of impact in affordable house delivery.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Harmonizing Innovation: Collaborative Synthesis of Bio-Silica Nanoparticles Derived from Rice Husk for Various Industrial Applications
descriptions: In a pioneering collaboration, we propose to join forces to establish a Research hub of Excellence. The heart of this project lies in the innovative synthesis of bio-silica nanoparticles, harnessed from rice husk, a sustainable resource abundant in Africa. These nanoparticles, with their unique properties, present a myriad of possibilities in industrial applications. From enhancing agricultural productivity to revolutionizing healthcare solutions, oil and gas etc; the potential of bio-silica nanoparticles is vast and transformative. A core objective of this collaboration is capacity building. Through rigorous research, hands-on training, and knowledge exchange, graduate students will acquire specialized skills related to nanomaterials and their diverse applications. This focus on skill development addresses the pressing issue of non-employability among graduate students in Africa. By empowering the future workforce with expertise in cutting-edge technologies, the project aims to bridge the gap between academia and industry, ensuring that graduates are not only knowledgeable but also job-ready. The Research Centre hub will drive innovative research, exploring the vast potential applications of bio-silica nanoparticles across industrial domains. Graduate students will receive hands-on training, enhancing their proficiency in nanomaterial synthesis, characterization, and application development. The project will foster collaboration between academia and industry, ensuring that research outcomes translate into practical solutions. By equipping students with skills relevant to industrial demands, the project aims to enhance employability, fostering a generation of skilled professionals ready to contribute to the workforce. By harmonizing innovation, enhancing skills, and fostering sustainable employment, this project strives to reshape the landscape of graduate education.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Development of CDIO (conceive, design, implement and operate) module/curriculum on Electric Vehicle Powertrains – Case study South Africa
descriptions: Revenue EV market is expected to show an annual growth rate (CAGR 2023-2028) of 16.86%, resulting in a projected market volume of £58.8m by 2028. Electric Vehicles market unit sales are expected to reach 1,413.00vehicles in 2028 in South Africa. The volume weighted average price of Electric Vehicles market in 2023 is expected to amount to £40.3k. The unemployment rate of young graduates aged 15–24 years fell from 40.3% to 32.6% in 2022, while it increased by 6.9 percentage points to 22.4% for those aged 25–34 years. Despite the engineering graduate unemployment being low in South Africa compared to other countries, there is still a gap in producing industry ready graduates to meet the growing market demand particularly in the automotive sector. In its updated NDC, South Africa has also set the goal to reach net zero emissions by 2050 in its Low-Emission Development Strategy. Reaching this target implies decarbonization of the transport sector which produces 43% of toxic emissions annually. The evolution of electric vehicles as possible replacement of fossil based powertrains will also require urgent need for curriculum and programme re - development to provide students with the needed skill to meet the existing skill gap in the automotive industry. This multidisciplinary curriculum will fill knowledge gaps, empowering recent graduates and seasoned engineers to drive the development of intelligent, zero, and ultra-low emission vehicles in the contemporary automotive sector. The main aim of this proposal is to develop the conceive, design, implement(CDIO) mode of a module on electric vehicles.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: A partnership to develop engineering and entrepreneurial capacity through the implementation of industry supported undergraduate programs
descriptions:
Waterborne disease kills more children than AIDS, measles, and malaria combined. This water problem is particularly acute in the urban regions across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where population growth is outpacing the development of supporting water infrastructure.

To solve this, new sustainable engineering solutions, major infrastructural programs, and technology-forward businesses have to be created. All of these initiatives require a well-trained, diverse, and empowered local engineering workforce, one that doesn’t rely on imported skills over the long term.

New student-centric initiatives that incorporate hands-on practical elements, provide skilled employment opportunities, facilitate engagement with industry, and real-world problem solving are needed to realize the potential of the engineering talent across SSA, thereby empowering communities to tackle big water problems.

This project focuses on the improvement of undergraduate engineering education in Tanzania. Specifically, it will create several hands-on industry-supported student dissertation projects to increase the impact of course curricula. An impact engineer training program will also be piloted - one that offers training in water engineering, human-centered design, and social entrepreneurship. Instead of short-term secondments, the pilot will then offer paid part-time employment opportunities, allowing the students to work as service engineers, supporting a local water kiosk operated by an industrial partner (Majicom). To create a sustainable framework a conference event and associated network for sharing of outcomes, learnings, and creation of new projects to ensure project sustainability.

In summary, the main aim is to improve undergraduate engineering education and employability via industry-relevant educational initiatives.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Enhancing the Learning Model and Opportunities for University Engineering Education (ELMO) (In partnership with Industry, UK and Regional Universities
descriptions: ELMO is a collaboration between the Engineering Faculty at the University of Sierra Leone (USL) and international regional partners. Faculty of Engineering in Sierra Leone as Hub is seeking to adopt into the curriculum a Problem Based Learning approach by students undertaking group research projects on industry’s identified significant challenges. Under ELMO, the academic tutors in Sierra Leone will work with the Industry Partner in defining research based thematic areas (primarily from the water supply, sanitation and energy sectors) in consultation with the UK partner and spoke universities in Africa.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: The Role of Engineers in Sustainable Watershed Management
descriptions: The proposed conference will focus on the roles that engineers can play in ensuring sustainable watershed management in Malawi and the Sub-Saharan Africa region. Watershed management's primary goals and objectives include approaching land degradation from a multi-facetted approach in order to maximize production, manage, control, and utilize water runoff, limit sediment production on watersheds, reduce the impact of rain on soil, optimize and sustain output while minimizing harm to natural resources and the environment. Unfortunately, engineers have shown limited attention to watershed management leaving this role to environmentalists. The conference will be held physically at the Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources (LUANAR). However, the conference will be streamed live to allow regional partners and others to attend remotely.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Kenya 2024 /2
descriptions:
Women around Lake Victoria face significant socio-economic challenges, exacerbated by the exploitative practice known as "sex for fish," where women are coerced into sexual relations in exchange for fish. This harmful practice not only compromises their dignity and health but also perpetuates poverty through unwanted pregnancies. Our project aims to empower these women by offering alternative sources of income, helping them break free from dependence on fish as their primary livelihood and reducing their vulnerability to sexual exploitation.
FAO 2020 revealed that women are willing to leave this trade if provided with alternative means of income. To address this we propose to empower women to earn money by harvesting water hyacinth and additionally engage in sustainable poultry and vegetable farming lowering women's reliance on fish, thereby avoiding exposing them to sexual exploitation. FAO further predicts that global poultry and vegetable consumption will increase by 25% by 2030, driven largely by the demand for organic, sustainable agricultural practices. Traditional farming methods face environmental and resource-related challenges, highlighting the need for innovative, climate-smart agricultural solutions due to enhanced productivity.
An internal market needs assessment and pilot study conducted by Biofit Feeds in 2020 demonstrated the willingness of women to participate in water hyacinth harvesting and a strong interest in the uptake of sustainable agricultural solutions, particularly those that address enhanced production and environmental concerns. Over 3 years WIDU Africa has supported over 100,000 green initiatives, which confirms the demand for sustainable, eco-friendly solutions. Through engagement with more than 10 LIF alumni, we have identified a growing demand for sustainable agricultural innovations in Kenya. LIF innovators working on eco-solutions have echoed the need for traceable, organic, and climate-smart solutions to address food security, environment and climate-related issues. Lake Victoria's green initiatives offer great potential to support women while simultaneously promoting LIF business by:
1/ LIF alumni will collaborate, leveraging their expertise to convert water hyacinth into valuable products. Women will earn by harvesting water hyacinth as raw materials for LIF companies. Finally, LIF companies will sell processed products to women farmers.
2/ Women will be capacity-built in sustainable green solutions in poultry and vegetable farming. This will enable women to earn income while creating a market for LIF innovations.
Lake Victoria's green initiatives showcase LIF-to-LIF collaboration in transforming invasive water hyacinth into valuable products and empowering women to leave the "sex for fish" trade creating long-term socio-economic opportunities and contributing to environmental sustainability.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: COMMUNITY GRANT KENYA 3
descriptions:
Leaders in Innovation Fellowship (LIF) program has offered enormous support to the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem in Kenya with many of the recent groundbreaking innovations in the country having been part of the program.
However, the program has not yet attained required level of publicity, commensurate to the potential of the program especially among researchers in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions and business incubators in Kenya. To this end, we propose to conduct a LIF Day in Kenya, with the aim of promoting the impacts of the LIF program in the country. This will be achieved by enhancing deeper collaborations among the local LIF community and also creating wider awareness of the LIF brand among upcoming innovators and entrepreneurs. We propose to hold the first LIF Day, Kenya in the year 2024 with a theme on climate action; Kenya launched their ambitious plan of planting 50 billion trees in November, 2023. A kick-off event will be done in February 2024. During the event, local LIF community members will come together to reflect on their milestones, challenges, and identify potential collaborations for business engagements. The LIF Day kick- off day event will bring together speakers invited from key organizations in the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem such as Kenya National Innovation Agency (KENIA), Research and Innovation Systems for Africa (RISA) and Ministry for Youth affairs and Creative economy, Kenya. The event will be face to face, to be held in Nairobi. Networking, discussion forums and Q & A session will be conducted. The LIF community will be sensitized to be very climate conscious in all their activities and voluntarily take part in the national tree planting activities whenever possible; as good role model of the society.
and subsequently followed be two workshops
After the LIF Day kick-off event, the LIF community will hold two virtual workshops in March 2024. One of the workshops will target the TVET institutions while the other one will target business incubation centers. Important topics on engineering technology, entrepreneurship and climate action will be presented by invited expert speakers and select LIF community members. Participants of the workshops will be drawn from engineering and science departments in local TVET institutions and incubators. Invitations for registration for the workshops will be sent through already established contacts at the target institutions. Participants will be enlightened on the need to convert knowledge and skills gained into practical scalable enterprises to solve societal problems. The proposed project will not only play a significant role in creating awareness about LIF programs, but will also sensitize, challenge and encourage the youth in Kenya to be more deliberate and intentional about innovation and entrepreneurship. The project will also help make participants more bold and intentional in preventing actions that would possibly cause or aggravate climate change. Lasting collaborative business engagements among the LIF community will be established and strengthened through the proposed project. Lasting creativity and entrepreneurial mind set will be triggered and enhanced among the participants of the project.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: COMMUNITY GRANT KENYA 4
descriptions: To grow, the Kenyan engineering community should leverage the strength of the diaspora. Over 100,000 Kenyan engineers spread across the continent represent a large network of potential development partners, and engineers' engagement with the diaspora is critical to closing critical development gaps. Multiple strategies are required for successful engagements, including building trust and partnerships (including securing investment in the diaspora by Kenyan engineers), investing in capacity building and knowledge sharing, and creating an enabling policy environment that recognises the diaspora's role in recognising sustainable development. KEDA's overarching goal is to provide a forum for intensive consultative interaction between Kenyan engineers, the diaspora, and other stakeholders, discussing viable solutions to the most pressing problems confronting Kenyan engineers and offering concrete strategies for needed partnerships. KEDA's mission is to integrate, harmonise, and synchronise various actions and programmes to promote the welfare and aspirations of Kenyan engineers and the diaspora. KEDA's goals are as follows: 1. Foster long-term relationships between Kenyan engineers and the diaspora, allowing the diaspora to invest in Kenyan innovations and increase diaspora remittances. 2. Give the Kenyan community the opportunity to tap into the diaspora's vast untapped potential to positively contribute to the socioeconomic development of Kenyan community engineering projects. 3. Allow the Kenyan diaspora to play a central role in shaping Kenya's sustainable development initiatives, and assist diaspora-led organisations in leading and implementing development projects in collaboration with Kenyan engineers.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: COMMUNITY GRANT KENYA 5
descriptions:
According to studies, 65% of children enrolled in primary schools today will have jobs that do not yet exist (World Economic Forum, 2020). It is further observed that although more girls are attending secondary schools today than before, they are significantly under-represented in STEM subjects and they appear to lose interest in STEM subjects as they reach adolescence stage. There is need to debunk the myths that girls do not like sciences. These trends can be reversed through investment in mentorship of girls at an early age together with inclusive innovation programmes.
Having recognized this gap, we as LIF alumni have initiated STEM Mentorship Programme in western Kenya, targeting secondary school girls. This will be a one-month intensive mentorship programme targeting 300 girls from informal settlement in Kisumu City. In addition, we identified the need to create awareness among science teachers on gender responsive pedagogy to enable them to sustain the interest of girls in STEM subjects beyond the project period.
This programme is unique in the sense that it encompasses all the facets of STEM mentorship with four main components.
1. Mentorship talks by STEM role models.
2. Exposing girls to the learning environment in the Institutions of Higher Learning.
3. Field visits for girls to the industry for experience of the actual application of STEM subjects in providing solutions to real life problems.
4. STEM is all about technology and innovation and there shall be incorporation of Science and Engineering Fair to expose female girls to the fun and beauty of engineering innovations.
Through this programme, more than 300 girls in over 10 secondary schools will be mentored. The overall objective of the project is to inspire girls to embrace science subjects with a view to enhance their participation in STEM courses and careers as well as engineering innovations. Specifically, the programme aims:
i. To inspire and nurture secondary school girls to see science as part of their lives and to embrace STEM fields for their future careers, while dispelling the myth that STEM courses are very difficult and a “no go” zone for women.
ii. To provide the girls with an opportunity to relate and interact with women scientists and engineering innovators for role modelling and mentorship;
iii. To educate secondary school girls on the admission requirements in engineering and science related courses in tertiary level institutions and to give them a clear view of the possible STEM professions that are available for them;
iv. To expose the girls to the learning environment at tertiary level institutions and especially for the different fields in Engineering, Applied and technology sciences;
v. To expose the girls to the work environment in the industries to help them relate what they learn in school to the real world of work and their daily lives through demonstrations and hands-on experience;
vi. To expose girls and their teachers to the beauty, fun and importance of STEM through Science and Engineering Fair.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Malaysia 2025 /1
descriptions:
This initiative aims to equip 30 educators, 10 each from underserved and rural communities in Malaysia, South Africa, and Brazil with practical skills in artificial intelligence and digital tools for inclusive teaching. Target participants include teachers from the rural communities in Malaysia such as Orang Asli, educators in South Africa’s townships and informal settlements, and teachers in underserved communities in Brazil.
The program will deliver culturally responsive training focused on AI literacy, digital pedagogy, and sustainability. Central to the initiative is the integration of the STEAM Club by SciEduc, a hands-on, eco-conscious learning platform developed by LIF Global 2025 innovator João Pedro da Cunha Molina. Educators will learn to implement STEAM Club projects using recycled materials and real-world challenges, fostering student engagement and environmental awareness with adaptation to local context in Malaysia and South Africa. This is further enhanced by co-developing and integrating AI and digital technology module to empower the educators in the teaching activities.
To promote global collaboration, the program will introduce a cross-border challenge problem. Educators from all three countries will be grouped into international teams to co-develop solutions using AI and STEAM methodologies, encouraging peer learning and intercultural exchange.
The main tasks are divided amongst the different country team members.  The Malaysian team integrates AI and digital tools such as generative AI and chatbots for lesson planning, embeds ethical technology discussions, and deploys adaptive learning platforms. The South African team shapes the global challenge by crafting real-world problem statements, designing scoring rubrics, and coordinating cross-border collaboration frameworks. The Brazilian team manages translations, localizing STEAM resources into Portuguese and other languages to ensure cultural relevance and inclusive communication.
There will be a hybrid and online 2–3-week training period with cross-country mentorship on digital and AI pedagogies, ethical technology use, adaptive learning strategies, and sustainability-focused approaches leveraging local eco-resources, followed by a global challenge sprint to bring educators together.
By empowering educators as agents of change, this project bridges the digital divide and cultivates a global community of practice committed to inclusive, tech-driven education

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Kenya 2024 /3
descriptions:
Kakuma refugee camp in Kenya is home to over 190,000 refugees from Rwanda, South Sudan, Congo and Somalia. According to GIZ Rapid Assessment Report, firewood accounts for 83% of the total energy consumption in Kakuma, while charcoal and kerosene account for 14% and 3% respectively. High consumption of wood fuel in Kakuma is responsible for 38% of the reported cases of respiratory diseases. Collecting firewood in unsafe locations leaves women vulnerable to Gender Based Violence from the host communities. Supply of cooking fuels in Kakuma is both humanitarian and market based. Every person is issued with 10 kg of free fuel wood rations every 2 months which is supplemented by purchased fuel wood. A GIZ study in Kakuma confirmed the ability and willingness of refugees to pay up to 15 USD per month to access clean cooking solutions. Likewise, there are over 338,000 residents living in informal settlements in Kisumu. Large proportions of these populations use firewood, kerosene and charcoal for cooking. About 56% of Kisumu residents rely on open stone hinged fireplaces as primary cooking energy source. This produces environmental degradation and exposure to health risks.
While there is potential market and willingness to pay for clean cooking technologies, LIF alumni still face critical challenges in accessing these markets. This includes low product awareness and poor distribution infrastructure leading to high delivery cost to these markets. This segment of the market is willing to switch to cleaner energy sources if awareness, affordability and reliability can be addressed, as revealed by a study done by International Finance Corporation.
Having recognized this gap, LIF-Kenya Alumni in the renewable energy value chain propose to conduct a Market Based Energy Access intervention project in these markets. The project team members have developed clean cooking technologies suitable for these markets. These technologies include bioethanol cooking fuel from Richard Arwa, ethanol fuel dispenser machines from Pascal Aloo, improved biomass cook stoves from Esther Were and electric pressure cookers from Evance Oketch among others. We propose consumer awareness creation with regards to our modern cook stoves and fuels. We shall do capacity development for Last Mile energy entrepreneurs to create business linkages between LIF alumni businesses and consumers within these markets. We shall advocate for policies that support clean cooking initiatives including subsidies, incentives and regulations that promotes use of clean cooking technologies. We expect increased sales of the alumni products due to increased awareness.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant South Africa 2025 /2
descriptions:
This project will host an immersive two-day inspirational event for five promising high school innovators — winners of the South African Youth Water Prize and Eskom Expo for Young Scientists — connecting them with up to 50 members of the South African and African LIF Alumni community. Exactly two decades ago, as a winner of these same prizes, I lacked the mentorship to see a clear path from youthful enthusiasm to a sustainable career in innovation. This project aims to bridge that exact gap by creating a more profound and impactful experience. By showcasing the real-world journeys of successful LIF alumni over two days, we will provide these learners with tangible role models, practical guidance, and a foundational network. The event will foster a collaborative environment where experienced innovators give back, strengthening the local LIF chapter and inspiring the next generation to pursue STEM fields as a viable entrepreneurial career, thereby seeding the future of South Africa, and Africa's, innovation ecosystem.

In my home language, Sesotho, spoken by around 13 million people, and understood by over 40 million in southern Africa in South Africa, Lesotho, Botswana, Zambia and Zimbabwe: "thupa e kojwa e sa le metsi' and it is a saying that loosely translates: 'the stick is bent while it's still green'. It is this philosophy that motivates this application so that we can show the young ones that innovation is a sustainable path, and a path to a sustainable future.

The primary goal is to start locally in person, with a virtual East African presence, as a pilot to having an annual and global event that inspires and recruits vibrant STEM talent.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: The Leaders in Innovation Fellowships (LIF) Innovator of the Year Award
descriptions: ShopOkoa is a product of deep creativity, rooted not in theory but in lived experience. In Kenya, millions of families survive on less than two dollars a day and are forced to buy food in small sachets that cost more per unit than bulk purchases. This creates a vicious cycle of premium poverty, where those with the least are charged the most. The result is chronic undernourishment, unstable household budgets, and little hope for financial mobility. The creative breakthrough came from transforming the traditional, informal shopkeeper credit system into a digital, structured, and intelligent platform. ShopOkoa allows families to purchase food in bulk and repay in small daily installments of less than one dollar. This approach lowers food costs by up to 25 percent annually and frees household income for other essential needs like rent, healthcare, and education. Our model blends community trust systems with artificial intelligence. We work through women-led savings groups called chamas, use AI to assess consumption patterns, and personalize credit limits. To scale sustainably, we introduced Microloan Backed Tokens, a financial innovation that enables individuals across the world to invest in African small businesses from as little as ten dollars. ShopOkoa does more than solve a problem. It reimagines how low-income families can access essential goods with dignity, stability, and long-term impact. It is financial infrastructure built from the ground up, using creativity to unlock opportunity where it matters most.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Uganda 2025 /1
descriptions:
The Engineering Innovation Bootcamp Uganda is a 6-week program that helps final-year engineering students prototype, test, and transform their projects into market-ready ventures, providing a clear path to commercialization with mentorship and training from LIF and Africa Prize Alumni, who have been trained by the Royal Academy of Engineering and pass on their knowledge and experience. Students will be selected from three government universities. The program addresses challenges highlighted in the Engineers for Africa 2025 report, produced by the Royal Academy of Engineering, including sub-Saharan Africa’s low engineer-to-population ratio (e.g., ~1 engineer per 30,000 in Uganda versus ~1 per 5,500 iSouth Africa), outdated curricula, limited practical training, and weak academia–industry linkages.

The bootcamp bridges the education-to-employment and education-to-entrepreneurship gaps by providing hands-on training in business modeling, pitching, and prototype development, complemented by mentorship from alumni and industry partners. To promote gender inclusion, all teams are led by female students, addressing the underrepresentation of women in engineering in East and Southern Africa (currently 8–14%).

Participants gain real-world exposure, develop viable products or services, and build networks connecting academia and industry. Post-bootcamp, students are linked to global entrepreneurship programs, including the Africa Prize, Echoing Green Fellowships and others, to accelerate scaling and commercialization.

Expected outcomes include training 100 students in 6 weeks, refining 20+ prototypes into commercial-ready ventures, establishing strong academia–industry partnerships, and creating a pipeline of female-led engineering startups.

By aligning engineering education with market needs, the bootcamp strengthens Uganda’s innovation ecosystem, enhances employability, and contributes to SDG 4, SDG 5, and SDG 9, fostering a generation of engineers equipped to solve local and regional challenges.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: COMMUNITY GRANT KENYA 2
descriptions:
Talent Forge is a digital collaborative network of Lif community members and engineering talent pipeline dedicated to propelling Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technology solutions to tackle sustainability challenges in Kenya. Bringing together individuals, entrepreneurs, companies, and universities, the platform places a strong emphasis on fostering collaboration and community support. Within this network, every Kenyan LIF participant is committed to giving back to the engineering community by assisting Kenyan students, with a specific focus on women in STEM, in overcoming challenges and advancing in their Fourth Industrial Revolution careers or as innovators. Participants earn network points for their contributions, which can be exchanged for valuable services, exposure, and mentorship opportunities. This approach aims to empower and support women in STEM, creating a pathway for their success in the evolving landscape of 4IR technologies.

Despite Africa's vast potential, women face significant underrepresentation in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) fields, particularly in Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technologies such as AI, data science, Virtual Reality, Space tech IoT, industrial internet of things, cloud computing, cognitive computing, and blockchain. This disparity impedes Africa's ability to fully harness the transformative potential of these technologies, as global studies indicate that only 26% of tech jobs are held by women, with an even lower representation in Africa. UNESCO reports that a mere 35% of STEM students in Sub-Saharan Africa are female.

Talent Forge is dedicated to bridging the gender gap by empowering over 300 female students with a strong interest in engineering from Kenyan universities, high schools, and TVETs. The initiative unfolds through a transformative three-week program, culminating in the Lif Community Innovation Day, conducted in collaboration with the Kenyan Lif community. This comprehensive program is meticulously designed to enhance skills in a broad spectrum of Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) technologies, including AI, data science, blockchain, virtual reality, augmented reality, computer vision, and space tech.

The climax on the Lif Community Innovation Day adds a significant dimension to the initiative, providing a dynamic platform for showcasing and celebrating the innovative outcomes of the program. It also serves as a moment to highlight and celebrate success stories within the Lif community, illustrating their impactful contributions to tackling sustainability challenges in Kenya. This inclusive approach emphasizes not only skill development but also the collective achievements and advancements made by the Lif community in addressing critical issues in the country.

In partnership with emerging tech companies from the Lif Community in Kenya, Talent Forge establishes pathways for female students to access job opportunities and apply their skills to address global challenges. This initiative recognizes the pivotal role of emerging technologies in Africa's future and aims to equip young women to become leaders in shaping the continent's 4IR landscape.

As an integral part of the project, the three-week program that will be conducted in Kenya, offers a unique opportunity for female students to engage in hands-on learning, drawing inspiration from the Lif community's experience. This immersive experience encourages innovation around various 4IR technologies, fostering collaboration and skill development.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Brazil 2025 /1
descriptions:
Organic waste is one of the largest contributors to landfills and a major source of greenhouse gas emissions. At the same time, it represents an underused resource that can be transformed into clean energy and biofertilizers. Public schools, especially those serving underserved communities, face the dual challenge of managing organic waste and providing students with opportunities to engage with sustainability.
This project proposes to turn schools into living laboratories of circular economy by building and operating biodigesters. Students will learn how organic waste from the school kitchen can be converted into biogas for cooking and biofertilizers for gardens. The project also incorporates entrepreneurship by encouraging students to sell surplus biofertilizer. Developed in partnership with a public school Science Club and its community, the initiative combines hands-on science education, ensuring that students not only learn STEM concepts and entrepreneurship, but also explore sustainable business models and see their direct impact.
The project methodology includes building small-scale biodigesters with students, documenting best practices to share with other schools in Brazil and abroad. The biogas produced will fuel the school kitchen, while the biofertilizer will be tested in school and community gardens. Throughout the project, students will co-develop impact models, interact with entrepreneurs and engineers from the LIF Alumni network, and join workshops on innovation, sustainability, and business development.
The model is designed for replication and scale, positioning education as a driver of sustainability. The long-term vision is to establish schools as hubs of inclusive, community-driven solutions to climate and social challenges.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Vietnam 2025 /1
descriptions:
I initiated the NetZero Study Tour - GreenLIF Network 2025 because I believe the green and circular economy must go beyond theory, it must be lived, experienced, and collectively built. As a founder working at the intersection of sustainability, innovation, and community, I’ve witnessed many passionate efforts by LIF alumni and local changemakers. Yet these efforts often remain fragmented, disconnected from each other and from the communities most impacted by climate change.

Vietnam and Southeast Asia face urgent environmental challenges - plastic pollution, food waste, unsustainable agriculture but also possess deep local wisdom and innovation potential. I saw a unique opportunity to connect top-down expertise from LIF alumni with bottom-up grassroots solutions emerging from villages, women cooperatives, youth-led startups, and circular agriculture pioneers.

This project was born from a simple yet powerful idea: turn the journey itself into the model. By traveling together, working side-by-side with local actors, and embedding circular principles into the entire tour-from food to logistics-we don’t just talk about systems change, we become it.

I want to lead this project to weave a stronger, more resilient LIF community that continues long after the tour ends. One that uplifts lived experiences, incubates cross-border collaborations, and co-creates new narratives of green development grounded in compassion, equity, and shared action.

This is more than a tour - it’s a seed for a regional movement.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Egypt /1
descriptions:
The "LIF tours Egypt: Empowering Academic Entrepreneurship Across the Nation" initiative aims to enhance academic entrepreneurship by expanding the Leaders in Innovation Fellowship (LIF) network throughout diverse and remote regions of Egypt. This project will engage academics, faculty, and students, as well as all commercialization and entrepreneurship enthusiasts, fostering collaboration and knowledge sharing while empowering participants with essential skills in technology commercialization and entrepreneurship.
Our primary objectives include expanding the LIF network, connecting stakeholders from various academic institutions, and strengthening the entrepreneurial ecosystem in Egypt. By conducting tailored events in key regions such as Alexandria, Suez Canal, Delta, and Upper Egypt, we will provide training workshops, roundtable discussions, and mentorship opportunities. Each event will cater to the unique needs of the target audience, ensuring maximum impact to expand the LIF network and set LIF alumni as experts among their communities.
Expected outcomes include increased visibility and recognition of the LIF Egypt Country Chapter, enhanced network diversity, established partnerships, and empowered academic entrepreneurs capable of translating research into viable products and services. We will measure success through key performance indicators such as the number of new LIF alumni participating in our activities and in the newly established Egypt chapter, collaborative projects initiated, and positive media coverage.
The project will be executed in three phases: planning and preparation, event execution, and follow-up and evaluation. We will leverage local partnerships, including collaboration with the Arab Academy for Science and Technology and other universities in different regions, to ensure successful outreach and diversity.
While potential risks include limited participant interest and funding challenges, proactive strategies such as targeted outreach and co-funding exploration will be implemented. The initiative also presents opportunities for scalability and sustainability, including the potential to expand to additional regions, foster collaborations with government and private sectors, and create a centralized knowledge repository.
Ultimately, the "LIF tours Egypt" aims to stimulate economic growth, improve societal quality of life, and enhance educational opportunities, contributing to a robust entrepreneurial ecosystem that empowers future innovators across Egypt.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Kenya 2024 /4
descriptions:
Carbon trading has become the new frontier for nature-based solutions globally. Carbon market is attracting a lot of interest due to its potential in offsetting carbon emissions for governments and being a source of revenue for businesses. Kenya has become a major player in carbon market, with Africa’s first verifiable carbon market having being launched in Nairobi, Kenya.
Many Kenya LIF alumni are working in projects that contribute to climate-action. LIF projects in agriculture, waste management, renewable energy, clean energy, e-mobility, and transportation stand a chance to benefit from the carbon market by broadening their revenue streams and accelerating efforts for climate-change mitigation.
With the carbon trading being a new front, many businesses lack the know-how for leveraging in the opportunity. Capacity building on carbon trading among innovators, entrepreneurs and corporate institutions is therefore urgently needed.
In light of this, LIF Kenya Chapter proposes to hold a capacity building training on carbon-credit trading for LIF alumni and non-LIF Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) in Kenya. The project aims at building knowledge on carbon trading and help participants take part in opportunities available in carbon market. The proposed LIF Connect project also aims to reconnect Kenya LIF-alumni across different cohorts and sectors, to network, and forge new collaborations. Activities of the project will help promote growth of the newly launched Kenya LIF Chapter.
The project will comprise three workshops; two online and one physical workshop. Participants will be trained on estimation of carbon emissions, calculation of carbon-credits, carbon trading platforms available, carbon pricing, carbon audit, and digital tools for calculation of carbon emissions. Sessions of the events will involve PowerPoint presentations, panel discussions, focus groups, Q&A, round table discussions, and networking sessions.
The training will be conducted by experts from institutions in the carbon emissions and climate-sector. Officials from Ministry of Environment, Climate Change & Forestry (MoECCF), Kenya National Innovation Agency (KENIA), British High Commission (BHC), and potential investors will be invited.
Project events will be published through media channels to help create awareness of the LIF community and promote the LIF brand and the Academy.
Enhancement of carbon trading skills will help accelerate investments and spur innovations in the climate sector. Participants will gain knowledge on how to leverage on carbon trading for additional revenue in their enterprises. The project will also contribute towards establishment of new partnerships between participating institutions, carbon-trade experts, the LIFalumni and the non-LIF SMEs.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Indonesia 2025 /1
descriptions:
"This project is a two-day intensive collaboration forum designed to reconnect and activate Indonesia's 54 LIF alumni, culminating in a public exhibition of their SDG-aligned innovations. The primary goal is to build a robust, cross-cohort support network by moving beyond informal networking to structured, facilitated collaboration.  

Day 1 is dedicated to internal community building. It begins with a Cohort Connect and  Challenge Mapping workshop, where alumni will identify shared local challenges and map their collective expertise. This is followed by a community dinner to deepen personal connections. 

Day 2 transitions from internal strategy to external impact, where alumni will pitch their project ideas formed on Day 1. This pitching session will be held within the the public exhibition, which serves as a platform to showcase original innovation that leads to collaborative solutions to the community, generate public engagement, and attract potential partners.

Outputs include a tangible list of alumni-led project concepts and a follow-up collaboration tracker. The project is designed to create a sustainable support ecosystem for Indonesian innovators."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community grant South Africa 2025 /1
descriptions:
Digi Library Hub is a collaborative community project that addresses critical educational access gaps at Sithokomele Primary School in Ratanda Township, Heidelberg, Gauteng. The project connects 500+ learners (Grades R-7) to knowledge through an innovative dual approach: a mobile library system and a digital learning hub powered by ICT telecommunications technology.
Ratanda Township faces significant educational challenges, with limited access to books and digital learning resources. Many learners lack exposure to reading materials beyond their textbooks, while digital literacy skills essential for 21st-century success remain out of reach for most township children.
Our solution combines physical and digital literacy interventions. The mobile library component will provide 200-300 age-appropriate books with a take-home lending system, fostering reading culture and family engagement. The digital learning hub will deliver internet connectivity through microwave radio frequency technology, providing 15-20 tablets loaded with educational content and enabling learners to develop essential digital skills.
This project leverages the expertise of 3  - 5 LIF South Africa alumni across ICT infrastructure, education technology, software development, and community engagement. Makhoba Professional Services, an ICT telecommunications company, will lead the initiative by providing connectivity infrastructure and overall project coordination.
Digi Library Hub directly contributes to SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) by democratizing access to learning resources and bridging the digital divide in underserved communities.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: COMMUNITY GRANT EGYPT 3
descriptions: As a member of the Alumni Advisory Council, the main objective of the current proposal is to achieve its main role of enhancing the alumni engagement with the academy and to increase their participation in its activities. In addition, the proposal aims to help with the council's goals -identified as higher priority- in the action plan. Improving the visibility of the AAC and developing a framework for collaboration within country partners are on top of such objectives. Accordingly, the current proposal is designed to organize a one-day conference-style event for the LIF community in the hosting country and the LIF cohorts in the neighborhood to show out their achievements. This can help with networking and will provide an appropriate context for all the LIF alumni in the same country (region) to meet in person. At the same time the in-country partner will be represented in the event to celebrate with the alumni their successes. Activities will include introduction of the AAC, in country partner briefing of its contribution to the LIF program, success stories of some examples of the LIF alumni, and a short message from the LIF champions. In parallel the LIF alumni will apply to showcase their products/innovations and to share insights with attendees and stakeholders. As many members of the AAC as possible will be applied with this same proposal independently. All AAC applicants will share the same event details and procedures. A long-term benefit for the AAC is building its own data base.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: COMMUNITY GRANT THAILAND 1
descriptions:
The upcoming project aims to revitalize collaborative engagement within the local LIF community, fostering stronger connections and providing tangible benefits. After nearly two years since the last formal community meeting supported by RAEng, this initiative will reintroduce in-person networking, creating a platform for alumni to reunite and fortify their relationships.

One key element of this project is a showcase designed to catalyze potential collaborations in both business and research among LIF members. This interactive event will serve as a nexus for exchanging ideas, fostering innovation, and exploring synergies within the community. By presenting opportunities for collaborative ventures, the showcase seeks to enhance the overall cohesion of the LIF community.

To further enrich the experience, distinguished speakers will be invited to share insights on topics crucial to the growth and development of LIF alumni. These thought leaders will provide valuable perspectives, encouraging intellectual discourse and offering strategic guidance for individual and collective business advancement.

Additionally, the project aims to broaden the scope of engagement by inviting key stakeholders such as PMUC, NSTDA, TRSI, and the British Embassy Bangkok to participate. These entities will have the opportunity to not only speak but also exhibit their projects, exclusively tailored to support the LIF community. By showcasing external initiatives, the project seeks to forge connections between LIF members and influential organizations, fostering an environment conducive to collaboration and mutual support.

The presence of these esteemed organizations will not only enhance the credibility of the event but will also provide LIF members with unique insights and resources that can significantly contribute to their professional growth. By curating content specifically relevant to the LIF community, the project aims to create a more focused and impactful collaborative environment.

In summary, this project is poised to rekindle the spirit of collaboration within the local LIF community. Through in-person networking, a collaborative showcase, insightful speakers, and engagement with key stakeholders, the initiative aims to strengthen the bonds among LIF members and provide them with a platform to explore new opportunities, both within the community and in collaboration with external partners.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Philippines 2025 /1
descriptions:
The BIO-LINK Project serves as groundwork for establishing a community-based enterprise in biomass utilization, with a primary focus on biochar production and application. In agricultural economies such as the Philippines and Malaysia, vast quantities of residues from rice, corn, coconut, and sugarcane remain underutilized or are burned in fields, leading to greenhouse gases emission and wasted resources. This project transforms that challenge into opportunity by co-developing pathways where residues are converted into biochar to improve soils, generate income, and contribute to climate action.

The project is uniquely positioned through the expertise of the lead applicant and co-applicant, who are actively exploring biochar applications across diverse fields including wastewater treatment, catalyst development for chemical manufacturing, energy, biostimulant production, and specialty products like inks. This breadth of applications ensures that farmer-level biochar systems are connected to wider innovation and market opportunities.

A critical element of sustainability is the active participation of farmers and cooperatives, whose input on biochar production will shape practical and scalable systems. Through crash courses, focus group discussions, and validation workshops, farmers will co-design enterprise models that directly benefit their livelihoods.

To sustain momentum, the project will establish a LIF Philippines–Malaysia Alumni Biochar Innovation Working Group. This group will convene LIF alumni, farmers, cooperatives, and partners to ensure that outputs—such as the Biochar Enterprise Roadmap—are implemented within a reasonable timeframe, bridging innovation with community adoption.

In the long term, BIO-LINK seeks to catalyze sustainable waste management, strengthen farmer enterprises, and position biochar as a driver of green growth and regional collaboration.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant South Africa 2024 /1
descriptions:
The proposed project aims to enhance community safety in Gqeberha, South Africa, by deploying innovative IoT security devices developed by Yunga Technologies. Led by three LIF Global Innovators—Bandile Dlabantu, Anatoli Kirigwajjo, and Linah Maphanga—this initiative addresses the high crime rates and deep-rooted social challenges in Gqeberha, particularly in its townships, where historical inequalities, unemployment, and social disintegration contribute to widespread criminal activity.

The project focuses on three core objectives: (1) deploying 20 Yunga IoT security devices in high-crime areas, (2) strengthening collaboration between the community and local law enforcement, and (3) training and empowering community members to actively participate in crime prevention. Yunga’s devices will enable real-time alerts and foster a network of vigilance, helping residents respond swiftly to potential threats. By integrating technology with community policing, the project aims to create a safer and more connected environment.

A key component of the project is enhancing trust and cooperation between the police and the community. Linah Maphanga, with her extensive background in law enforcement and community organization, will lead efforts to build these relationships, ensuring that the project’s impact is both sustainable and far-reaching. The project will also empower residents by providing them with the knowledge and tools to protect their neighborhoods, fostering a sense of ownership and responsibility for their safety.

The project is aligned with the Royal Academy of Engineering’s values of progressive leadership, diversity and inclusion, excellence everywhere, collaboration first, and creativity and innovation. It represents a bold and collaborative approach to tackling crime, leveraging the strengths of each partner to drive positive change in Gqeberha.

The project is designed to be implemented over three months, from September to December, with a detailed plan outlining responsibilities, outcomes, and measurements at each stage. The project’s success will be measured through a reduction in crime rates, improved community-police relations, and the effective use of Yunga devices by residents. This initiative offers a scalable model for enhancing community safety in other high-risk areas, with the potential to make a lasting impact on Gqeberha’s social fabric.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Kenya 2025 /5
descriptions:
This project brings together LIF Alumni to empower indigenous smallholder farmers in Teso, western Kenya, through improved post-harvest handling and guaranteed market integration. Peanuts are a key livelihood crop in the region; however, farmers lose 30–40 percent of their harvests due to poor drying, shelling, and storage. Furthermore, up to 60 percent of locally sold peanuts are contaminated with aflatoxin (Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service (KEPHIS), 2023). These losses reduce incomes, threaten health, and block access to premium markets.
We will pilot a participatory training program with 100 smallholder farmers, at least 70 percent of whom are women and youth, focusing on solar drying, safe shelling and grading, hermetic storage, and aflatoxin prevention. A culturally tailored, illustrated toolkit co-developed by farmers and technical experts from the LIF Community and Ministry of Agriculture, blending modern engineering innovations with indigenous knowledge, will guide training. Validation will be done through farmer focus groups, extension officers, and food safety specialists to ensure accuracy, usability, and cultural resonance. Demonstrations at MAMLO FOODS’ peanut micro-factory will reinforce skills and link practice directly to processing.
Trained farmers will be contracted to supply peanuts to the micro-factory, securing them a stable offtake market. Lessons from the pilot will be documented to refine the toolkit and inform a scalable model for other peanut-growing regions in Kenya and beyond.
By the end of the project, we expect a 20 percent reduction in post-harvest losses and a 30 percent reduction in aflatoxin contamination. More importantly, we will establish a replicable, community-driven model that integrates food safety, income generation, and engineering innovation for long-term continuity.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Kenya 2024 /1
descriptions:
The Revolutionize Engineering UpLIFT Her Communities project is a transformative three-week initiative focused on closing the gender digital divide for young women from marginalized and low-income communities in Nairobi, Kenya who are in business but lack the necessary digital skills, resources, and formal business training to compete in today’s market due to limited access to education, early pregnancies, and economic hardships. This project, organized by the Kenyan LIF Community in collaboration with the Kenya National Chambers of Commerce and Industry, and supported by engineering student bodies such as the Google Student Developer Club at Kenyatta University, IEEE, and Kenyatta University Female Students in Tech, seeks to empower these women by integrating their businesses into the digital economy.

One participant poised to benefit is Nadia, a young woman from the Mathare slums. Nadia's journey into entrepreneurship began after she was forced to drop out of school due to an early pregnancy and the economic hardships that followed. She started a small business making and selling peanut butter from locally sourced groundnuts and honey. Despite her hard work and determination, Nadia's business has struggled to thrive due to a lack of formal business training and a nonexistent digital presence, which are crucial for competitive success in today’s digital-driven marketplace. The project integrates these women’s businesses into advanced digital platforms developed by the LIF Community in Kenya—such as ShopOkoa, Biz Mkononi, Vertical Farms, and Sanitary Dispensers—while also incorporating e-commerce solutions from TikTok Shopping and YouTube Shopping and providing training in business and personal branding, ensuring they not only establish a strong digital presence but also gain the operational efficiency and market reach necessary to thrive in today’s competitive environment.

With approximately 13,000 girls dropping out of school annually in Kenya due to similar challenges, this project is poised to make a significant impact. By focusing on Fourth Industrial Revolution technologies—such as AI, IoT, blockchain, and data analytics—combined with e-commerce and branding tools, the project equips participants with the ability to enhance their economic potential and reduce the income inequalities that have long affected their communities. Through this initiative, the LIF Community will strengthen its network, amplify its impact, and establish itself as a leader in addressing gender and economic inequities in Kenya, while contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals of gender equality and economic empowerment. The initiative will culminate in a Mental Health and Wellness Day for the women and the LIF Community.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: COMMUNITY GRANT KENYA 1
descriptions:
The proposed project, titled "Food Systems Dialogue leveraging Engineering for Climate Change Mitigation," led by LIF alumni Irene, aims to address critical issues in Western Kenya's food systems through innovative and collaborative efforts. The project aligns seamlessly with the objectives of the LIF Community Grant Programme, focusing on building impactful networks, fostering collaboration, and positively influencing local communities.

The central theme of the project is to bring together a diverse group of stakeholders from various sectors, including county government, banking institutions, research organizations, academia, food activists, and engineering associations. This collaborative effort is geared towards addressing the multifaceted challenges posed by climate change in the Western Kenya region, particularly within the context of food systems.

The project's core components include a one-day "Food Systems Dialogue" in Kisumu, drawing in 100 participants with expertise spanning county governance, finance, research, academia, activism, and engineering. This dynamic gathering will serve as a platform for innovative discussions, idea exchange, and problem-solving, with the overarching goal of leveraging engineering solutions to mitigate the impacts of climate change on local food systems. The engagement of stakeholders from multiple sectors is designed to foster cross-sectoral collaboration, echoing the LIF Community Grant Programme's emphasis on professional collaboration between alumni cohorts and diverse sectors.

Irene's localized knowledge of the Agri Food SME landscape in western Kenya is a cornerstone of the project's success. Building on her previous experience in convening stakeholders for access to finance discussions, she understands the unique challenges faced by local businesses and aims to apply this knowledge to the broader context of climate change and food systems. This targeted approach ensures that the proposed project is not only relevant but deeply rooted in the specific needs and opportunities of the Western Kenya Region region.

Anticipated outcomes include the establishment of new and qualitative business connections within the LIF network and beyond, with a focus on engineering-led solutions for climate-smart agriculture. The project aims to engage a significant number of LIF participants, encouraging them to take on leadership roles within their sectors and communities. This active participation aligns with the objective of developing communities of LIF alumni positively impacting local communities and enhancing the visibility of the LIF brand.

"Food Systems Dialogue leveraging Engineering for Climate Change Mitigation" project is poised to make a substantial contribution to the development of the LIF alumni network. The project's potential to create lasting impact, foster cross-sectoral collaboration, and address critical challenges in Western Kenya's food systems aligns seamlessly with the overarching goals of the LIF Community Grant Programme. This initiative is not only an opportunity to drive positive change but also to elevate the visibility of the LIF brand in the Western Kenya Region.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Kenya 2025 /3
descriptions:
The Maasai Mara national game reserve is a unique wildlife conservation haven, famous for its spectacular natural diversity of wildlife. The game reserve is a home to a large number of Lions, Cheetah, Elephant, Rhino, African Buffalo, Wildebeest, Giraffe, Zebra and many more. Furthermore, the game reserve has been voted as one of the new Seven Wonders of the World.  However, many species in this ecosystem are either endangered or facing extinction due to unsustainable charcoal burning by the local communities.
Large proportions of the local population use fuel wood and charcoal as primary cooking energy sources. This does not only produce environmental degradation and exposure to health risks but also leads to human-wildlife conflicts by accelerating deforestation and habitat destruction which results into animal displacement, starvation, and death, pushing many wild animals into human settlements and farms in search of food and water. This encroachment results in crop raiding, livestock predation and direct danger to humans. 
Based on this background, LIF-Kenya alumni in collaboration with Kenya Wildlife Service, propose to promote adoption of clean energy technologies developed by LIF alumni to provide households with affordable clean cooking and lighting energy systems while mitigating human-wildlife conflicts within Maasai pastoralist community. 
The specific interventions shall include:
1. To organize community forums to raise awareness about clean energy and to explain the link between charcoal use and human-wildlife conflicts to secure project buy in.
2. To select 100 vulnerable households in human-wildlife conflict prone areas for piloting. Each household will contribute $ 10 as part of co-ownership while they will receive one clean cook stove, fuel, training and after sale support.
3. To deploy LIF alumni products such as Solar Predator Deterrent Light, a flashing LED lights that mimic human movements and help to keep away predators at night. Other technologies include Cook&Light, a dual purpose kits for cooking, lighting and charging phones; bio-ethanol fuel and solar pressure cookers among others.
4. To organize a one day interactive exhibition with all LIF alumni innovations on display. The purpose of the demo will be to showcase benefits, build momentum and recruit more households for scale up beyond project period.

This proposal aligns with Kenya’s national goals on climate action, wildlife conservation and clean energy access. By empowering local communities with sustainable alternatives, the project will help preserve Maasai Mara ecosystem while enhancing the livelihoods and safety of the people who live around it.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Kenya 2025 /1
descriptions:
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global public health menace caused by overuse and misuse of antibiotics in human and veterinary medicine, agriculture, and aquaculture. AMR makes disease causing pathogens like bacteria resist against the medicine used in treating diseases, making infections difficult or impossible to treat. The antimicrobial compounds used in food-producing animals often belong to the same classes as those used in human-medicine. Given the overlap, there are growing concerns that extensive use of antibiotics in animal farming could contribute to the development of resistance to antibiotics in human-medicine.
Intervention measures to contain the spread of AMR are therefore urgently needed in order to protect human, animal, and environmental health.
LIF Alumni Community in Kenya consists of talented innovators and entrepreneurs, some of whom are knowledgeable and experienced on ideal ways of tackling antimicrobial-resistance. The innovators believe that creating awareness and strengthening stewardship on use of antimicrobial compounds would go a long way in reducing spread of AMR. 
Therefore, LIF Alumni Kenya Chapter proposes to conduct a capacity building workshop on antimicrobial stewardship among poultry and livestock farmers in Kenya.
The aim is to sensitize and train the farmers on responsible use of antibiotics in their farms to curb the growing AMR menace. This will also be an opportunity for the LIF alumni to apply skills and experiences gained through the LIF program in tackling pressing societal needs.
Women poultry and livestock farmers from different farmer communities in Kiambu and Nairobi counties in Kenya will be invited to apply for workshop-participation and 30women-farmers selected to attend the workshop as representatives of various farmers’-groups.
Members of LIF Alumni Kenya Chapter will lead the larger Kenyan-LIF-community in organizing and implementing the project in collaboration with AMR experts from the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock and the Ministry-of-Health, Kenya.
The project will entail a one-day physical workshop to be held in January, 2026 in Kiambu County.
Interactive sessions including roundtable-discussions, PowerPoint-presentations, case-studies, storytelling, networking, and Q&A will be used to train the farmers on best-practice in management of farm-animals to reduce AMR.
The project will be of utmost significance to the LIF Kenya Chapter, becoming part of annual target Chapter activities. It will help bring together Chapter-members and other LIF-alumni to reconnect, engage, network, and grow the Chapter membership.
The farmers will become empowered with knowledge and skills for eliminating misuse and overuse of antibiotics, while improving animal health and increasing productivity.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Kenya 2025 /4
descriptions:
The Tilting the Scales project aims to close the gender gap in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education by focusing on the Junior Secondary stage (Grades 7-9). Girls and boys in Kenya perform equally well in primary science. However, their participation sharply differs as they transition to high school. By senior high school, fewer than 40% of girls take science subjects, while more than 78% of boys do. This gap continues into higher education and the workforce, where women make up less than one-third of the STEM labour force.
This disparity shows obstacles related to exposure, mentorship, and encouragement, not ability. Girls often face stereotypes, limited role models, and a lack of confidence, which can reduce their interest in STEM subjects. Kenya’s Competency-Based Curriculum (CBC) has created opportunities in pure sciences, applied sciences, and engineering at the Junior Secondary level, yet girls’ participation drops at this crucial point. The project aims to inspire and support girls at this stage to reverse this trend.
The initiative will focus on 300-400 girls in two major Junior Secondary schools in Uasin Gishu and Elgeyo Marakwet counties from November 2025 to February 2026. Activities will include STEM Career Days with hands-on workshops, motivational talks, and mentorship from 10-15 professional women in STEM, including Leaders in Innovation Fellowship (LIF) Alumni. Through these sessions, girls will see how classroom learning connects to real-world applications and meet relatable role models who thrive in STEM careers.
To promote sustainability, mentorship will be integrated into the existing science and math club, while interested students will be linked with mentors. All participants will also learn about STEM opportunities available for girls, such as those through the Royal Academy of Engineering, including the LIF Fellowship, Africa Prize for Engineering, LIF women, and related programs, which will expand their view of what is possible in STEM careers.
By creating welcoming platforms that boost confidence, support mentorship, and expose girls to global opportunities, this project will increase STEM participation in the schools and contribute to Kenya’s industrial growth and sustainable development.
