agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Indonesia 2025 /2
descriptions:
"From Wastewater to Waves of Life is a collaborative initiative led by LIF alumni Septian Suryo (PUFFER Smart Water System, LIF4/2018), Awan Rimbawan (KLH Bioreactor, LIF4/2018), and Ferry Sugandhy (Monster Group IT Solution, LIF5/2019) to address the environmental challenges of shrimp aquaculture while creating new economic value for coastal households. The initiative applies a closed-loop approach in which wastewater from shrimp ponds is treated and repurposed as a growth medium for land-based seaweed farming. This reduces marine pollution while generating a sustainable product with both economic and ecological benefits.
The project will commence in Takalar District, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, one of the country’s most intensive shrimp-farming centers, spanning over 4,000 hectares of ponds. Discharges from these ponds, containing high levels of nitrogen and phosphorus, have been linked to seawater degradation and reduced ecosystem resilience. Seaweed farmers in the area also experience unstable growing conditions due to poor water quality. By integrating PUFFER’s wastewater treatment, KLH’s bioreactor for nutrient stabilization, and digital aquaculture monitoring tools, the project creates a system that transforms waste into a productive resource.
During the pilot stage, the system will process roughly 1,000 m³ of effluent to support 0.5 hectares of land-based seaweed cultivation. Expected results include the production of around 3-5 tons of fresh seaweed, engagement of 30 coastal farmers (at least 40% women), and at least 30 % reduction in organic pollution in pilot sites. Additionally, seaweed biomass will capture an estimated 1-2 tons of CO₂ equivalent during the project period, contributing to local climate resilience.
By combining engineering innovation with community engagement, this initiative demonstrates how technology can strengthen the circular blue economy, improving water quality, restoring marine ecosystems, and supporting sustainable livelihoods in coastal Indonesia."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: COMMUNITY GRANT  EGYPT 2
descriptions:
ENGAGE aims to share best practices to support technology commercialization in the water sector through organizing a networking/stakeholder event in Egypt for LIFers Cross-cohort and Cross countries (virtual) to identify potential gaps in the water treatment sector and propose a collaboration between industry, academia, and governmental bodies to leverage the expertise from LIF and allocate resources. The networking event targets LIF participants working in water treatment from different Cohorts, however interested LIFers are welcome to share their experiences. The event will take place over 3 days and will be divided into four activities: Talks by LIFers about their journey from the LIF program where they are now, we aim to discuss topics such as start-ups in Egypt, prototyping, iterations, licensing, and IP for water technologies and how to overcome the commercialization of relevant products. A hands-on training on pitching and storytelling for industry, round table discussions, and finally an onsite visit at Port Said to visit a water treatment project. The main participants of this event will be LIFers cross-cohort from Egypt, with invitations for virtual participation to our fellow LIFers to discuss water problems in other regions and how to benefit from each other’s experiences and motivate those who completed LIF program but lost the enthusiasm to continue their entrepreneurship journey. The Lead applicant (Ola Gomaa, LIF Global 2023), Co-applicant (Irene Samy, LIF 5) along with Sherif Abou El Enien (LIF Global 2023), Mohamed Aly (LIF Global 2023) and Mohamed Farouk Abdel-Kader (LIF6) are key team members who will participate in organizing the event activities, and the on-site visit to Port Said. During the event, one LIF mentor will be invited to provide mentorship and give advice about ways to overcome bottlenecks facing LIF entrepreneurs. Invitations will be extended to a shark tank winner, and the manager of NilePreneurs, Nile University to enrich the discussions. This will be done through the following:
1-Share best practices and success stories of commercialization through demonstration of different products from LIFers
2-Develop a targeted marketing strategy to highlight the unique features of water treatment technologies and related management technologies to emphasize the competitive edge of LIFers
3- Discuss funding opportunities from private investors, and venture capital to support research, development, and initial commercialization efforts.
4- Discuss end-user education and different routes to increase commercialization in different regions
5-Identify robust monitoring and evaluation to track the performance and impact of the proposed technologies.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Kenya 2025 /2
descriptions:
"The COVID-19 pandemic exposed deep gaps in student-welfare across higher education systems, with 264 million students globally, including 9 million in sub-Saharan Africa, facing disruptions and 56% battling food insecurity (UNESCO, 2020; Owusu et al., 2022). Budgets existed, yet support rarely reached students quickly or transparently, forcing many to dropout. Most institutions still rely on paper forms, manual vetting, and slow audits, fragmenting responsibility and delaying help during crises like pandemics. This leaves 200 million students—particularly those with disabilities, orphans, and low-income backgrounds—at risk of dropping out due to chronic hunger and financial shocks. In Kenya, female students face exploitation, with some pressured to trade sex for necessities like sanitary pads, exposing a structural failure, where student-welfare systems lack speed, inclusion, and accountability, rendering vulnerable students invisible and unsupported (FAO, 2022).

This project equips universities and TVETs with a Blueprint to deliver fast, inclusive, and auditable student-welfare powered by ShopOkoa's Fintech Technology. 

ShopOkoa will help Universities to digitize student welfare departments end-to-end and use AI on consented admissions records to identify learners likely to need support, including students with disabilities, medical needs, orphaned students, and those from low-income backgrounds. After eligibility is confirmed, student-welfare offices can issue virtual prepaid cards in the ShopOkoa app to the verified students. The cards are configured with clear spend rules and are used to deliver cash assistance and targeted meal subsidies for essentials such as meals, groceries, sanitary pads, urgent health items, and emergency support to vulnerable students. Students can use the cards through the ShopOkoa mobile application and USSD on basic phones. Assistive features and delivery options ensure students with disabilities can access and use the service reliably, strengthening inclusion, speed, and operational efficiency. Administrators can monitor activity in real-time and generate policy and donor-ready reports from an immutable audit log.

With a £5,000 LIF Community Grant, we will deliver four workstreams. A policy and governance roundtable, which will align ministries, disability offices, and university leadership on consent, data protection, and audit. A practitioner masterclass, which will define the target operating model, standard operating procedures, service level objectives, and escalation paths. An architecture clinic, which will map integrations to student information systems and payments, and define role-based access control and segregation of duties. A hands-on sandbox, which will train welfare teams to configure spend-rules, onboard merchants, reconcile transactions, run incident drills, and demonstrate user journeys.

Outputs include a student-welfare digitization playbook for global-replication."

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: COMMUNITY GRANT EGYPT 1
descriptions:
COMMUNITY GRANTS PROMOTE LIF ALUMNI, ENTREPRENEURSHIP ACTIVITIES AND FUTURE INNOVATOR OUTREACH IN THE LIF COUNTRIES.  
Traffic accidents around schools constitute a significant portion of pedestrian accidents in developing countries, especially near schools situated along main roads where incidents are notably frequent. The lack of attention to the presence of school students exposes them to the driver's errors and sometimes to fatal consequences, permanent disabilities, or at the very least, psychological trauma.

The project will start by selecting a school in Heliopolis, Cairo, identified as the most critical location based on accidents reports and infrastructure issues using an innovative crowdsourcing APP “StreetKey”, which is an App founded by Ahmed Osama, an LIF 2023 alumni. The objective is to study the selected school's current situation, devise solutions, and implement quick-win interventions to mitigate risks and ensure the safety of students. Coordination with the selected school will be facilitated through a civil society organization “Heliopolis Heritage Initiative” in Heliopolis City . The analytics, visual inspection of the streets around the school and solutions design will be through a research center at Faculty of Engineering Ain Shams University, “Center of Mobility Research (CMOR)”, which another LIF alumni, Tarek Sabry, is among the management board.

CMOR and another NGO “Nada Foundation for Road Safety (NADA)” will collaborate to develop surveys assessing students' traffic awareness, identify surrounding risks, and create an awareness campaign curriculum. Afterwards, NADA will collaborate with relevant authorities through the civil society organization "Heliopolis Heritage Initiative" to implement simple engineering interventions to decrease risks.

Our project is committed to involving the local LIF community and their children in addressing the issue of road safety around schools. In addition of the involvement of two LIF alumni directly in the project, we will conduct workshops, and community meetings to raise awareness, gather feedback, and encourage active participation of the rest of the local LIF community and the various communities. By engaging the LIF and local community directly, we ensure that our solutions are tailored to their specific needs and challenges, fostering a sense of ownership and empowerment. Through this collaborative approach, we aim to create a stronger community that actively promotes road safety and safeguards the well-being of their children.

descriptions:

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Kenya 2024 /5
descriptions:
There is quite some growing alarm in Kenya over the rates of Suicide. Since 2020, the numbers of suicide cases have steadily risen, indicating a big problem. Daily media is littered with news of new cases of people taking their lives or causing serious harm to themselves. A lot of this can be attributed to economic frustration because of the need to make ends meet. While Kenya is a rapidly growing economy, it is quite a struggle to find meaningful employment opportunities or run businesses for many Kenyans. This causes stress and frustration among these people. A further consequence is that due to their limited financial status, they are unable to afford proper counseling.
The Kenyan government has taken a proactive stance by launching and supporting the Suicide Prevention Strategic Plan (2021 – 2026). However, more needs to be done. We believe that by helping people understand their mental and emotional well – being, they can achieve some awareness of their state of well being. This can help reduce the misconceptions and stigma around mental health. Further, we believe that we can collaborate in the development of a small toolkit that people can use to engage in some form of self-care. This would allow people to improve their mental and emotional well-being, and will be especially important for those who cannot afford or access conventional methods of getting help.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Malaysia 2025 /2
descriptions:
Leptospirosis is a bacterial zoonotic disease transmitted through water and soil contaminated with animal urine, particularly from rodents and cattle.  Leptospirosis deaths in Malaysia have fluctuated over the past two decades, with mortality rates ranging from 0.45 to 0.53 per 100,000 population and case fatality rates between 1.47% and 14.3% depending on region and period. Mortality is highest during and after major flooding events, in high-risk states such as Perak and Kelantan, and among older adults, males, and those with organ dysfunction or delayed diagnosis. Farmers are among the highest-risk groups in Malaysia due to frequent exposure to wet environments, irrigation channels, and livestock enclosures. Many remain only vaguely aware of the disease without fully understanding its transmission, symptoms, and preventive measures.

This project aims to strengthen awareness and prevention of leptospirosis among farming communities through a one-day targeted program. The initiative will combine education, demonstrations of protective gear and the use of technology tools to empower farmers with accurate knowledge and safe practices. The project will showcase our technology which is a portable sensor for detection of pathogenic leptospirosis in wastewater.  This allows early alert of the presence of hazardous pathogenic leptospirosis bacteria in the vicinity, allowing appropriate precautions be taken. This will help to reduce the risk of infection and allow containment of the disease. 

Awareness talks will be delivered in Bahasa Malaysia by health and agricultural officers will explain transmission routes, warning signs, and the importance of routine wastewater testing especially after a rainy or flooding event. Culturally appropriate educational materials, including illustrated leaflets and posters will be distributed using social media and during the seminar. Demonstration sessions will show farmers how to use simple protective measures such as boots and gloves, highlight safe water practices, and introduce effective rodent control techniques. Champions will be selected amongst the participants, for each respective farm. They will be empowered to train and monitor fellow workers.

To reinforce the message beyond the event, we will conduct visits two months after the event to evaluate the effectiveness of the workshop and if safe water practices are implemented on-site. Wastewater testing will also be demonstrated and conducted on the farmer's premise to solidify understanding and implementation. Expected outcomes include improved knowledge, increased adoption of protective practices, and routine wastewater testing behavior among farmers. Ultimately, the program aims to reduce leptospirosis incidence in agricultural communities, contributing to healthier and more resilient rural populations.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community grant Turkiye 2025 /1
descriptions: Smallholder farmers often lack access to affordable tools to track essential soil parameters such as moisture, pH, and nutrient levels. Our proposal introduces a low-cost sensor network deployed in pilot sites (cotton/wheat farms in Türkiye, rice/palm oil plantations in Malaysia, rice farms in the Philippines, and spice/vegetable farms in India), with data integrated into a cloud-based platform and accessible via a mobile application. Farmers will be trained to interpret sensor data and apply it in decision-making for irrigation and fertilisation. By leveraging the combined expertise of LIF Alumni in electronics, agriculture, and data analytics, the project will contribute directly to SDGs 2, 12, and 13 by promoting efficient resource use, reducing input costs, and enhancing climate resilience. The initiative will also foster knowledge exchange between farming communities across Türkiye, Malaysia, the Philippines, and India.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Community Grant Jordan 2025 /1
descriptions: This project deploys an AI-powered energy management system to provide reliable and affordable electricity to three double-shift girls' schools in northern Jordan, which also host a significant number of Syrian refugee students. By integrating IoT sensors, predictive analytics, and a student-friendly mobile app, the system will optimize energy use, reduce electricity costs by 30%, and extend power availability to support both school shifts and after-hours study. Piloted successfully in Azraq Refugee Camp, this solution will improve educational conditions for over 1,200 female students and refugee learners, enabling extended study hours, digital tools, and safe, well-lit facilities. The project supports SDGs 4, 5, and 7, with a scalable model for national expansion.

descriptions: To solve today’s most pressing development and sustainability challenges, academics need to work with industry, government and the public to build trust, design appropriate solutions and scale their uptake. The Transforming Systems through Partnership (TSP) programme achieves this by catalysing partnerships between universities, large companies, SMEs and start-ups to address sustainable development goals.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Reassuring the Safety of Treated Pharmaceutical Industrial Wastewater for Reuse in Jordan using Innovative Nature-based Solutions
descriptions:
This project will build upon and advance the achievements from the previous TSP project, which aims to obtain strong evidence supporting the use of innovative nature-based solutions to treat pharmaceutical wastewater for reuse in the context of water safety, economy viability and practical implementations. Two existing pilots will be monitored at industrial sites for one year, aligning with the Jordanian water reuse standard JS202/2007 (WP1). Antimicrobial resistance (AMR), a non-statutory parameter, can be generated during pharmaceutical treatment, creating barriers for safety reuse of the treated wastewater. This project will assess AMR as a proactive contaminant in treated effluent (WP2). Cost-benefit analyses will be conducted, and training courses on wetland design, operation, and troubleshooting will be provided to stakeholders to gain confidence for the implementations (WP3). Moreover, with the support of industry partners and governmental stakeholders, targeted supplementary fund will be sourced for full-scale technology implementations (WP4). Ultimately, the expected outputs of the project include,
• One scientific research article in peer-reviewed journal and a policy recommendation for Jordanian authorities.
• A technology prototype at TRL7 and trained staff for system operation.
• An application to USAID-IAF fund and an agreed plan with industrial stakeholders for real application.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Exploring the potential of Economic and Environmental Impact: Cost Savings throughout the Life Cycle of  Pre-installed Solar PV Panels employing Nanof
descriptions:
In Jordan, the demand for renewable energy, specifically solar power, has intensified due to environmental concerns and economic challenges. Despite widespread adoption of solar PV panels, there's a pressing need to enhance their efficiency and lifespan. Economically, reducing energy costs is crucial, considering its significant portion in national expenditure. By optimizing existing solar PV panels with innovative methods like nanofluid and water cooling, substantial cost savings can be achieved, aligning with economic goals and making renewable energy more accessible.

This study investigates cost savings in pre-installed solar photovoltaic (PV) panels using nanofluid and water-cooling technologies. The study employs a comprehensive economic analysis that encompasses installation costs, maintenance expenses, and operational expenditures. By comparing traditional cooling systems with nanofluid and water-based alternatives, this analysis reveals the economic feasibility and long-term financial advantages of adopting these innovative cooling solutions.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Low-Cost Manufacturing and Formulation via Sustainable Automated Reactor Platforms
descriptions:
Jordan faces challenges related to medication adherence, particularly among children, primarily due to the unpalatable taste of drugs. This challenge directly impacts healthcare outcomes and escalates long-term healthcare costs. Additionally, there is an increasing need for effective collaboration models between academia and industry to foster innovation and reduce the country's reliance on costly pharmaceutical imports.
The project's primary objective is to create cost-effective and sustainable technologies designed to enhance the adherence of pediatric patients to medication. This is achieved by reformulating medications with unpalatable tastes, a particularly important concern for infants, children, and elderly individuals who may encounter difficulties when swallowing pills. These specific patient groups require dosage forms that are tailored to their age, are palatable, and can consistently and precisely administer varying doses.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Integrating environmental technology solutions for developing a circular economy for olive mill waste system
descriptions: Improved management of the olive mill waste system, comprising mainly of olive mill wastewater (OMW) and solid pomace, is highly needed for Jordan’s rapidly growing olive industry and the country’s obligations to meet targets 6.3 and 6.6 of the UN Sustainable Development Goal-SDG6 on management of water and sanitation. This one-year UK-Jordan bilateral project builds on the successful progression of lab-scale evaluations from a previous Transforming Systems through Partnership project, which identified our proposed photo-Fenton (UV-assisted) OMW treatment technology showing high reduction potential for both phenols and Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) of over 99%. However, some key limitations in scaling the exact technology to service the volume of OMW treatment at industrial scale were noted, including the sludge build up on the solid phase catalyst influencing its efficacy during continuous operation; affordability of the technology (both capital and operational costs); reuse of recovered solid waste and treated wastewater. The main aim of this project is to overcome all three limitations by integrating complementary environmental technologies to make the operability of the photo-Fenton technology viable at industrial scale.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Transforming research outputs into industry tools and capacity in support of the National Flood Studies Programme in South Africa
descriptions:
This NFSP in South Africa was initiated by industry to update and modernize the use of old methods which are currently widely used in industry and which were developed using limited data, and to improve flood risk assessment capacity in industry. This resulted in the drafting of an implementation plan and budget for the NFSP. 
This project aims to
(i) To support national and international collaboration between academics and industry
(ii) To support communication and collaboration between researchers and industry
(iii) To develop flood risk assessment capacity in industry
(iv) Transform outputs from research undertaken by the NFSP to date into software tools and products for use by industry
(v) Collate and make accessible data, information and methods for flood risk assessment in practice

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Development and Implementation of Waste-Filled Portable Crash Boxes for Crashworthiness Performance Improvement of Road Service Vehicles
descriptions:
In 2021, rear-end collisions, which are the most frequent type of automobile accidents, account for 28% of all automobile accidents in Thailand. The fatal rate of rear-end collisions is high if one of the vehicles is significantly more rigid, e.g. a small vehicle against a heavy truck. Statistically, 60-70 people are annually dead in Thailand due to the rear-end collisions of the mismatched vehicle.
This project aims to (i) design two different waste-filled portable crash boxes for road service vehicles, (ii) implement waste-filled portable crash boxes for at least three road service vehicles from different owners, and (iii) disseminate knowledge on sustainable-designed crash boxes to the public.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Fostering Clean Energy transition in Jordan Utilizing Energy Storage Technologies and integrating Demand Side Management
descriptions:
The energy transition in Jordan, marked by a significant increase in the adoption of renewable energy sources and the integration of low-carbon technologies like electrified transport and heating, has presented grid operators with several pressing challenges. These challenges include the need to address issues related to low system inertia and grid congestion while ensuring the continued supply security, maintaining power quality, and preserving system stability. By 2030, The government aims to have 50% energy share from the renewable, the forecasted Electric Vehicles in 2030 will be 500,000 vehicles.
With this significant change, there is a need for hybrid integrated solutions combined the energy storage solution and demand side management to operate the electrical system in efficient and reliable manners. The previous project (TSP2021\100334) has focused on the economic and environmental roles of ESS in Jordanian. Our motivation for pursuing the current project stems from the feedback and insights gathered during our previous efforts. This proposal encompasses various facets related to capacity building in energy storage, demand side management, grid stability, and leverages the existing energy storage system for valuable lessons and insights

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Unlocking the Potential of Alternative Building Technologies and Informal Construction Strategies in Sustainable Housing Provision
descriptions:
South Africa faces significant challenges in the housing sector, with a large backlog in housing supply and a high demand for affordable housing. According to the South African Government's Housing Development Agency, as of 2020, there is a backlog of approximately 2.1 million houses. This backlog is particularly prevalent in informal settlements, where many poor urban populations reside.

The project examines how new materials (specifically alternative building technologies - ABTs) can be integrated into the supply chain to address conventional materials' limitations and enhance sustainable housing provision. It also seeks to examine and improve the informal housing construction practices of urban poor communities. With the demand for affordable housing increasing and a significant housing supply backlog, it is important to find sustainable solutions that can reduce the housing backlog while still being affordable.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: MEASUREMENT OF RESIDUAL STRESSESES AND  POROSITY STUDIES ON CORROSION RESISTANCE OF PROTECTIVE COATINGS FOR OFFSHORE WIND TURBINE FOUNDATIONS USING TH
descriptions:
Thailand, like many other countries, is aggressively making the transition to sustainable energy sources. In this transformation, the offshore wind energy industry is essential. Thailand is a desirable location for the development of wind energy because of the Gulf of Thailand's vast offshore wind potential.
This study's main goal is to assess how well thermal spray coatings work as a preventative measure for onshore and offshore wind turbine foundations i.e., Monopile. The inquiry covers a wide range of topics, such as the measurement of residual stresses, the influence of coating porosity on corrosion, and simulations of corrosion resistance. Synchrotron X-Ray Diffraction (S-XRD) will be used to evaluate residual stresses that result from thermomechanical processes and microstructural phase changes.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Bytes over Lights: Levelling up community connectivity with cost-effective optical wireless communication
descriptions:
Unfortunately, in countries such as South Africa, ubiquitous affordable, reliable, and fast internet connections remain a dream. In South Africa, 95% of the population has 4G internet coverage, yet 40% of households cannot afford it. This issue is exacerbated by the fact that mobile data becomes cheaper with larger purchases. For instance, a 15GB data bundle costs 15% of the income of a low-income household. This starkly contrasts with the global internet cost benchmark of 2%.

There's no universal solution for internet access. Our project aims to narrow the divide by collaborating with existing technologies. Partnering with RIOT Network and PeCo Power, we'll use our innovative optical wireless technology from the previous TSP project to boost RIOT's community WiFi network pilot projects, making them faster, more reliable and more economically viable. Our devices will utilise PeCo’s solar power solution, ensuring consistent operation, crucial during South Africa's frequent blackouts.

With this foundation, we plan to:

- Install our prototypes into RIOTs pilot network: Upgrade then integrate our prototypes to improve RIOTs pilot community network.
- Deploy network telemetry: Acknowledging the distinct internet needs of each locale in terms of content accessibility, language, and relevance, we will employ privacy-conscious, industry-standard network telemetry to gain insights into how the community uses their internet connections.
- Publish a roadmap to “reasonable” internet access: Using insights gathered from the previous output as well as engagement with various stakeholders, we will lay a foundation for the future.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Sustainable Monitoring & Advanced Real-Time Energy Efficiency (SMARTEE): Pioneering IoT Submetering in Pharma Manufacturing
descriptions:
The SMARTEE project aims to enhance energy management in the industrial sector by leveraging advanced IoT-based electrical monitoring systems. Collaborating with industry, innovation center, and academic partners from the UK and Jordan, the project will design, develop, and deploy a tailored submetering system, facilitating real-time energy insights and promoting efficient energy consumption.
Through a series of visits, workshops, seminars, and apprenticeship programs, the project will foster knowledge exchange, upskill professionals, and engage students in hands-on experiences. The joint research initiatives will further analyze energy data, providing actionable insights to optimize energy usage.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Fabrication of nanosilver doped activated carbon into high-efficiency car air filter
descriptions:
Outdoor air pollution stands as one of the most significant environmental threats to public health in Thailand, presenting a substantial challenge that affects the well-being and prosperity of individuals. In response to this critical challenge, there is an urgent need for air filtration solutions capable of mitigating these pollutants, thereby enhancing the quality of life for individuals and populations.
Our current achievement includes the successful development of green sustainable and scalable production process for silver-doped activated carbon (Ag/AC), operating at 150-liter initial feed capacity, corresponding to a TRL-6. The resulting Ag/AC material serves as a highly effective adsorbent, proficiently eliminating gases and has remarkable efficacy in inhibiting bacteria and viruses.
Therefore, this project is committed to broadening the applicability of Ag/AC by pioneering accessible technology to produce air filters, with a particular focus on upscaling production (TRL-6 to higher level). Additionally, we intend to conduct field tests to evaluate their performance in public transportation.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Empowerment of people with disabilities through integration of eco-energy systems and sustainable garment processing (Eco-ubulumko)
descriptions:
South Africa is suffering from economic downturn and energy poverty, that is leading to scheduled load shedding to reduce the overall demand. Not only that, the electricity generation is mainly prone to coal-fired power plants, therefore, it is not environmentally friendly, and not helping the country to achieve their low carbon target. Therefore, investment in renewable energies at small and large scales is the preferable way out. Where this project is giving a solution for clean energy at small scale.
People with disabilities are normally at risk and marginalised in many communities in Africa and SA is not an exception. They are isolated and work in high risk areas. This project is building on the seeds of caring for people with disabilities in the fashion industry to support these families and provide safe and clean environment for them to be part of the community and live a decent life.
This project is designed to harnessing the power of engineering to build sustainable society & inclusive economy that works for everyone, through coupling the developed technology of hybrid renewable energy sources to power the upcycling and downcycling processes of garments established by families and micro businesses

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Hydrogen-Based Green Engine Enhancement
descriptions:
To transform the transport sector in Jordan towards a more sustainable and cleaner future, this project will develop a technology that works with internal combustion and diesel engines to reduce pollutants, fuel consumption, and efficiency. Hydrogen fuel has the potential to achieve this, but liquifying hydrogen requires a lot of energy, and the facilities for hydrogen supply in Jordanian cities are limited. This project generates Hydrogen by implementing electrolysis reactions. The hydrogen-oxygen (HHO) combination is then fed into the combustion chamber, potentially reducing emissions and improving efficiency.
Irbid, the largest city in northern Jordan, with a population of over 1.7 million, will be targeted as one of its municipality's selected mobile engines will be used to install the developed technology to enhance engine efficiency and reduce harsh emissions, as well as get public engagement, enabling potential implementation for other local authorities in Jordan to support Jordan's National Green Growth Plan. To achieve this added value in engine performance, the project will include thorough process modeling to decide on design parameters and optimize the HHO unit and capacity for different engine ranges, the development of a prototype that can be used for real-world testing to measure NOx, HCs, CO, CO2, and O2 emissions, and analyzing power and fuel consumption. The main project’s outputs will be mapped to the TSP program objectives as follows:
• Develop an innovative HHO generator technology that could be integrated with engines to improve efficiency and minimize pollution in the transport sector.
• Set a new partnership between Yarmouk University and Ferasah in Jordan with Aston University in the UK to develop new collaborative engineering courses and implement the CDIO framework.
• Delivering public awareness and engagement activities to ensure buy-in from local authorities and to upskill the working force to allow further implementation of the technology.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Affordable hearing for all: Mobile remote AI software to access hearing and predict cognitive decline among older adults
descriptions:
World Health Organization suggests all adults aged over 50 should undergo hearing screening. They are at 1.94 times higher risk of developing dementia and need to receive prompt intervention. In Thailand, this population is equal to over 20 million older adults. Hearing evaluation and screening needs not only advanced medical equipment but also well-trained medical personnel such as audiologists, audiovestibular medicine physicians etc., which Thailand lacks. However, over 90% of older adults in Thailand can access mobile phones and applications. Using remote mobile technology can help not only create affordable hearing screening health but also increase accessibility for older adults in remote areas. We partner with an industrial partner who received the TSP funding in 2021 with advanced software and mobile application technology in both Android and iOS systems to conduct hearing screening and evaluation.
Main outputs of this project 
1. Evaluate the AI algorithm of the mobile application to conduct hearing testing without human supervision.
The result with be compared with medical-personnel lead standard testing environment
2. Access the acceptability of Thai older adults/community in using the mobile hearing screening application.
The community in Thailand suburbs will use the application to self-test their hearing. The acceptability of the application in the community will be explored.
3. Analyse for the best predictors of hearing ability among Thai older adults
The database from the mobile application will be analysed to identify the most appropriate test condition.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: TUT & UoS Solar vehicle engineering project: building on prior success
descriptions:
South African and Africa at large is impoverished and is in dire need of clean and more affordable transport mechanisms. Similarly, South Africa does not have a strong automotive in-house sector, which has the potential to create thousands of jobs if we can for instance start to produce our own local vehicles. South African students also have a lack of modern scares skills, especially in the electric vehicle sector.
This continuation project will build on knowledge and skills obtained from the previous collaboration and aim to develop a more sustainable clean energy transportation prototype (with two seats) by ensuring systems and sub-systems adhere to the South African Bureau of Standards for future homologation of the solar electric vehicle in the L7 category (mass and traction power restriction only) which should enable further funding towards possible commercialization.

titles: A transformative staff enhancement project for implementation of innovative integrated engineering curricula across SA HE institutions

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Biogas Empowerment: Accelerating Community Grids and Collaborative Networks in Thailand (BEACON)
descriptions:
In Thailand. there is a strong demand for clean and affordable alternative fuels, which BEACON seeks to address by enabling sustainable biogas energy systems, which involve actors and stakeholders currently excluded from the dominant biogas paradigms. 
Firstly, it seeks to increase biogas yields by identifying and assessing optimal combinations of feedstocks for co-digestion. Secondly, it aims to analyse the practicality and economic viability of implementing community-level biogas grids, tailored to the specific contexts and needs of Thailand. Finally, the project intends to facilitate the long-term adoption and success of these technologies by focusing on stakeholder engagement and robust knowledge transfer, realised through targeted educational and collaborative activities

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Novel micro-monolith reactor for efficient conversion of waste CH4 and CO2 into valuable chemicals using renewable electricity
descriptions: The project fits the industrial, social and government demands in Thailand (in terms of environmental and clean energy goals) which are to encourage the 'low-carbon credit society' and 'circular economy'. This project, if successful, will give a significant impact on environment, energy security, well-being of locals, education and economy. In terms of innovation, this project is original and novel. There are limited recent publications on how to co-valorise waste methane and CO2 to value-added chemicals and fuels using renewable electricity so far. From my opinion, this project is innovative and aligns with Thailand 4.0 policy and BCG model (bio-circular-green economy), launched by Thai government.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Catching them young through Sibo the Engineer Project
descriptions:
Following the resounding success of Sibo the Engineer Project in the Africa Catalyst Phase 4, and the huge appetite for the project amongst other PEBs in Africa and beyond, this project will meet the objectives of the Africa Catalyst programme by firstly communicating, disseminating and exploiting the successes of the pilot project in the initial kickoff meeting with the selected PEBs. Secondly, the project will facilitate targeted capacity-building workshops for the PEBs so that they in turn have the ability to build up an engineering talent pipeline with the necessary skills to respond to local challenges, creating strong professional engineering bodies in sub-Saharan Africa. Third, two additional Sibo the Engineer children's books, an ECD STEM activity book and two animated series will be produced. Fourth, the PEBs will create and implement early and middle childhood STEM education programs in their respective regions with the guidance and monitoring of the project, and form industry partnerships. This project contributes to the diversity and inclusion objective of the call by targeting girls and promoting gender equity in STEM. It will address ethnic, socio-economic, and gender disparities in STEM fields by creating inclusive and diverse STEM education content for early childhood, available in digital form for a wider reach. Critical to this project will be the continuous monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning aspect of the projects to be developed and implemented. A report will be compiled at the end with recommendations for other PEBs and government education departments for reference and adoption.
Stakeholders are WFEO, FAEO education and capacity-building committees, PEBs in sub-Saharan Africa, education departments, industry.Lessons learnt from the previous rollout is importance of getting industry and government buy-in from early stages for sustainability of the projects. This will be heavily emphasised during the rollout of the different projects by the PEBs.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Raising Public Awareness and the Profile of Agricultural Engineering to Grow and Sustain Agricultural Engineering Professional Engineering Bodies in A
descriptions: Food, water and energy insecurity are widespread throughout Africa. Technologies to promote food, water and energy security can be developed by Agricultural Engineers, hence there is a significant need to grow the Agricultural Engineering profession in Africa. Building on the successes and recommendations from completed African Catalyst projects by the project team, it is envisaged that further support for PASAE and national AE-PEBs will promote and grow the profession of Agricultural Engineering in Africa, which is necessary to provide the skilled human resources and technology for improved and sustainable water supply, food production, food processing, food storage and environmental management. This will promote the food, water and energy security required to meet the growing population, both in Africa and internationally, and thus support the reduction of poverty in rural marginalised communities.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Empowering Professional Engineers for Career Success
descriptions: The purpose of this project proposal is to outline a comprehensive training program for young graduate and women engineers in Rwanda, focusing on preparing them for job interviews and equipping them with the necessary skills and knowledge to effectively navigate, succeed in the marketplace as well as successfully transition into their chosen industries. By partnering with UK partner, HR firms and industry stakeholders, International Engineers Rwanda will conduct public lectures, offering comprehensive training and implementing various methodologies to bridge the gap between academic qualifications and industry requirements, ultimately enhancing the employability and career prospects of graduate and women engineers.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Engineering Excellence Alliance - Strengthening engineering professionalism, capacity, and growing engineering talents for sustainable development in
descriptions:
The Engineering Excellence Alliance seeks to address critical challenges within Sub-Saharan Africa's engineering landscape focusing on strengthening professional engineering bodies, building organizational capacities, and nurturing engineering talents for sustainable development. The project responds to the pressing need for cohesive and effective structures within the engineering profession, recognizing the pivotal role engineers play in driving economic growth, innovation, and social progress

Sub-Saharan Africa faces a multifaceted engineering landscape characterized by fragmented professional bodies, inconsistent standards, and a gap in skills alignment with industry demands. The project acknowledges the necessity for a unified and empowered engineering community capable of addressing contemporary challenges, driving policy advocacy, and setting robust standards for engineering education and practice.
Moreover, there is a need to bridge the gap between academia and industry, ensuring that engineering education aligns with practical industry demands. The project recognizes the potential of collaboration between professional bodies, educational institutions, and industry stakeholders to foster knowledge exchange, skill development, and the seamless transition of engineering graduates into the workforce.

Gender inclusivity and diversity in engineering remain critical challenges. The project aims to actively address these issues by promoting initiatives that attract, retain, and upskill women in engineering, creating a more inclusive and diverse professional environment.

Additionally, the focus on youth engagement and STEM education responds to the imperative of nurturing a pipeline of engineering talents from a young age. By promoting STEM education in schools and providing opportunities for hands-on experience and mentorship, the project aims to inspire the next generation of engineers and ensure a sustainable flow of skilled professionals into the industry.

The Engineering Excellence Alliance is motivated by the need to create a cohesive, empowered, and forward-thinking engineering community in Sub-Saharan Africa. By addressing fragmentation, enhancing professionalism, and nurturing talent, the project aspires to contribute significantly to the region's sustainable development.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Integrated and Inclusive Infrastructure Framework (3iF) - Phase 3: Professional development for Kenyan engineers on urban development principles, tact
ntegrated and Inclusive Infrastructure Framework (3iF) - Phase 3: Professional development for Kenyan engineers on urban development principles, tacti
descriptions:
East Africa is one of the world’s most rapidly urbanising regions. The expanding informal settlements often sit at the confluence of climate risk, poverty, political contention, and a lack of basic infrastructure provision. These neighbourhoods also hold vast potential to shape a new and viable urban future.

In Kenya, residents and civil society organisations deliver basic services in low-income areas, at the same time as major infrastructure investments take place across cities. While legislation and many current and planned “slum upgrades” emphasise investment in infrastructure, the question remains: how should these systems be planned and designed to bring real change to residents?

The Integrated and Inclusive Infrastructure Framework (3iF) was conceived on the idea that if infrastructure investments are inclusive of all voices and needs, and integrate physical, social, and ecological systems, they can create just, resilient, and viable neighbourhoods and cities. 3iF is a pair of practical resource guidance (the ‘Practice Guide’ and the ‘People’s Guide’) that aims to maximise the integration and inclusivity benefits of various efforts to improve informal settlements in Kenya.

3iF was developed through an extensive co-production process with government, academia, and civil society organised by a group of leading practitioners, thinkers, and doers in this space in Kenya. It used an impact-focused research approach to develop, test, and disseminate a set of principles and tactics designed to make infrastructure an integral catalyst for improving a broad range of social, economic, and health-related goals.

The ‘Practice Guide’ was developed to support government, built environment professionals, students and academics for developing policy, and planning, engineering, designing and implementing infrastructure upgrading projects.
The ‘People’s Guide’ is a practical guide for communities and CSOs which provides guidance on how to engage with, understand, and participate in infrastructure and informal settlement upgrading projects.
The third phase of the 3iF project aims to build on the considerable interest, engagement, and momentum achieved in its first two phases to share and communicate the Framework in Kenya, to train the future engineers of Kenya, to expand to other East African professional bodies, and to create impact in real world infrastructure projects. In the last two years 3iF has emerged as a set of tools that facilitate participatory planning and engineering for a viable urban future among diverse stakeholders, including the private sector, government, and civil society. These tools, coupled with real-world applications, are designed to support institutional and professional learning across the built environment professions. The framework's success to date in real-life projects demonstrates its relevance in addressing sustainable infrastructure investment challenges in urban Kenya. A key addition in this phase is the Institution of Engineers of Kenya (IEK), alongside the Architectural Association of Kenya (AAK), with the overlapping Engineering Chapter of AAK.

agency: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
titles: Strengthening the Institutional Framework of UIPE to advance the Contribution of Engineering Professionals to Innovation Value Chain in Uganda
descriptions:
UIPE seeks to strengthen the Innovation capacity of Engineering Innovators starting with 3rd and 4th year students from selected Universities across the country as well as developing the IP and innovation policy for the institution.
UIPE is very passionate about diversity and inclusion in the way it delivers services to its members as informed by the diversity and inclusion policy developed during the GCRF phase 2. Therefore in this project UIPE seeks to reach out to marginalized groups specifically women in engineering and engineers with disabilities.
In addition, the project will also set up and train an engineering innovation peer review committee that will continue to receive and review innovation prototypes.
